chase-cps 0.5.0
built with pdoc

chase_cps

CHASE: Contract-based Heterogeneous Analysis and Systems Exploration.

Python interface to the CHASE core library and its back ends::

from chase_cps import Contract, refines

spec = Contract.from_strings(inputs=["req"], outputs=["grant"],
                             assumptions=["G F !req"],
                             guarantees=["G (req -> F grant)"], name="Spec")
impl = Contract.from_strings(inputs=["req"], outputs=["grant"],
                             guarantees=["G (req -> X grant)"], name="Impl")
result = refines(impl, spec)    # valid, or invalid with a counterexample

The package has three layers:

  1. Contracts and their algebra (chase_cps.contract): the contracts, and the operations that build contracts from contracts (compose, conjoin, disjoin, merge, divide, separate, imply, coimply, invert, saturate, assume, ensure), computed by the CHASE core library. They do not depend on a theory or a back end. Contracts are read and written in the logics language of CHASE (parse_spec, to_spec) and in SystemVerilog Assertions (parse_sva, to_sva, see chase_cps.sva).
  2. Checks (chase_cps.checks and chase_cps.logic): the checks on contracts (refines, verify, is_compatible, is_consistent, is_implementation, is_environment, is_receptive, remove_redundant) reduce to queries on formulas of a theory (implies: validity; is_satisfiable: satisfiability; unsat_core), which the back ends decide (nuXmv, NuSMV; real variables through chase_cps.reals). The implementations and environments can be state machines (chase_cps.models).
  3. GR(1) synthesis (chase_cps.gr1): realizability, synthesis, and the analyses built on them (unrealizable_core, is_well_separated, is_vacuous, and remove_redundant with synth=True), for contracts in the GR(1) fragment of LTL, with slugs.

All the names are also available from chase_cps itself.

@dataclass
class Contract: 
 69@dataclass
 70class Contract:
 71    """An assume-guarantee contract.
 72
 73    ``assumptions`` and ``guarantees`` are lists of LTL formulas, read as
 74    conjunctions. Variables are Boolean ("bool"), bounded integers
 75    (low, high), or reals ("real").
 76    """
 77
 78    name: str
 79    inputs: dict[str, VarType] = field(default_factory=dict)
 80    outputs: dict[str, VarType] = field(default_factory=dict)
 81    assumptions: list[ltl.Node] = field(default_factory=list)
 82    guarantees: list[ltl.Node] = field(default_factory=list)
 83    # How the contract was computed: (operation, operands), set by the
 84    # operations of the algebra (see _recorded); chase_cps.viz draws it.
 85    origin: tuple | None = field(default=None, compare=False, repr=False)
 86
 87    # Construction ------------------------------------------------------------
 88
 89    @classmethod
 90    def from_strings(cls, inputs=None, outputs=None, assumptions=None,
 91                     guarantees=None, name: str = "C") -> "Contract":
 92        """Build a contract from formulas in the standard LTL syntax.
 93
 94        >>> c = Contract.from_strings(inputs=["req"], outputs=["grant"],
 95        ...                           assumptions=["G F !req"],
 96        ...                           guarantees=["G (req -> F grant)"])
 97        """
 98        c = cls(name=name, inputs=_normalize_vars(inputs),
 99                outputs=_normalize_vars(outputs),
100                assumptions=_normalize_formulas(assumptions),
101                guarantees=_normalize_formulas(guarantees))
102        c.validate()
103        return c
104
105    @classmethod
106    def from_pychase(cls, pc, shared=()) -> "Contract":
107        """Convert a contract of the CHASE core library. ``shared`` are the
108        declarations of the system (outside the contracts) that the contract
109        may use."""
110        from ._native import representation as R
111        inputs, outputs, generic, constants = {}, {}, {}, {}
112        for d in list(shared) + list(pc.declarations):
113            name = d.getName().getString()
114            t = d.getType()
115            kind = type(t).__name__
116            if kind not in ("Integer", "Boolean", "Real"):
117                raise ValueError(f"{name!r} has the type {kind}: only Boolean, integer, "
118                                 "and real variables are supported")
119            if type(d).__name__ == "Constant":
120                constants[name] = ltl.number(d.getValue().getValue())
121                continue
122            # A real without a range has the bounds -+infinity of the core library
123            # (the largest int64).
124            if kind == "Real" and (t.getMin() > -_UNBOUNDED or t.getMax() < _UNBOUNDED):
125                raise ValueError(f"{name!r} is a real with a range: write the range as an "
126                                 "assumption or a guarantee instead")
127            if kind == "Integer":
128                vtype = (t.getMin(), t.getMax())
129            else:
130                vtype = "real" if kind == "Real" else "bool"
131            causality = d.getCausality()
132            if causality == R.causality_t.input:
133                inputs[name] = vtype
134            elif causality == R.causality_t.generic:   # e.g. a proposition, inlined
135                generic[name] = vtype
136            else:
137                outputs[name] = vtype
138
139        def value(node):    # constants are replaced by their values
140            if isinstance(node, ltl.Var) and node.name in constants:
141                return ltl.Num(constants[node.name])
142            if isinstance(node, ltl.Unary):
143                return ltl.Unary(node.op, value(node.arg))
144            if isinstance(node, ltl.Binary):
145                return ltl.Binary(node.op, value(node.left), value(node.right))
146            return node
147
148        def terms(domain_map) -> list[ltl.Node]:
149            out = []
150            for domain, spec in domain_map.items():
151                # the formulas only: the DSL also puts its architecture there, as a graph
152                if type(spec).__name__ == "Graph":
153                    continue
154                out.extend(value(t) for t in ltl.conjuncts(ltl.from_pychase(spec)))
155            return out
156
157        assumptions, guarantees = terms(pc.assumptions), terms(pc.guarantees)
158        used = ltl.variables(ltl.conjunction(assumptions + guarantees))
159        outputs.update({k: v for k, v in generic.items() if k in used})
160        return cls(name=pc.getName().getString(), inputs=inputs, outputs=outputs,
161                   assumptions=assumptions, guarantees=guarantees)
162
163    def validate(self) -> None:
164        for n in [self.name] + list(self.variables):
165            if n in RESERVED or not n.replace("_", "a").isalnum() or not n[0].isalpha():
166                raise ValueError(f"{n!r} cannot be used as a name: names start with a "
167                                 "letter, contain letters, digits and _, and are not "
168                                 f"keywords of CHASE ({', '.join(sorted(RESERVED))})")
169        both = set(self.inputs) & set(self.outputs)
170        if both:
171            raise ValueError(f"variables both input and output: {sorted(both)}")
172        declared = self.variables
173        for f in self.assumptions + self.guarantees:
174            missing = ltl.variables(f) - set(declared)
175            if missing:
176                raise ValueError(f"undeclared variables {sorted(missing)} in "
177                                 f"{ltl.to_str(f)!r} (contract {self.name})")
178        if words.has_words(declared):
179            for f in self.assumptions + self.guarantees:
180                try:
181                    words.check(f, declared)
182                except words.WordTypeError as e:
183                    raise ValueError(f"{e} (in {ltl.to_str(f)!r}, contract {self.name})") \
184                        from None
185
186    # Views -------------------------------------------------------------------
187
188    @property
189    def variables(self) -> dict[str, VarType]:
190        return {**self.inputs, **self.outputs}
191
192    @property
193    def assumption(self) -> ltl.Node:
194        return ltl.conjunction(self.assumptions)
195
196    @property
197    def guarantee(self) -> ltl.Node:
198        return ltl.conjunction(self.guarantees)
199
200    @property
201    def saturated_guarantee(self) -> ltl.Node:
202        """A -> G."""
203        if not self.assumptions:
204            return self.guarantee
205        return ltl.Binary("->", self.assumption, self.guarantee)
206
207    def to_dict(self) -> dict:
208        def t(v):
209            return v if isinstance(v, str) else list(v)
210        return {"name": self.name,
211                "inputs": {k: t(v) for k, v in self.inputs.items()},
212                "outputs": {k: t(v) for k, v in self.outputs.items()},
213                "assumptions": [ltl.to_str(f) for f in self.assumptions],
214                "guarantees": [ltl.to_str(f) for f in self.guarantees]}
215
216    @classmethod
217    def from_dict(cls, d: Mapping) -> "Contract":
218        def t(v):
219            return tuple(v) if isinstance(v, list) else v
220        return cls.from_strings(
221            inputs={k: t(v) for k, v in (d.get("inputs") or {}).items()},
222            outputs={k: t(v) for k, v in (d.get("outputs") or {}).items()},
223            assumptions=d.get("assumptions") or [],
224            guarantees=d.get("guarantees") or [], name=d.get("name", "C"))
225
226    def __str__(self) -> str:
227        lines = [f"CONTRACT {self.name}"]
228        for k, v in self.variables.items():
229            kind = "input" if k in self.inputs else "output"
230            lines.append(f"  {kind} {k} : {v if isinstance(v, str) else f'{v[0]}..{v[1]}'}")
231        lines.append("  Assumptions:")
232        lines += [f"    {ltl.to_str(f)}" for f in self.assumptions] or ["    true"]
233        lines.append("  Guarantees:")
234        lines += [f"    {ltl.to_str(f)}" for f in self.guarantees] or ["    true"]
235        return "\n".join(lines)
236
237    # CHASE core library ------------------------------------------------------
238
239    def to_logics(self) -> str:
240        """The contract in the logics language of CHASE (as read by logics_tool)."""
241        found = sorted(v for v, t in self.variables.items() if words.word_type(t))
242        if found:
243            raise ValueError(f"word variables ({', '.join(found)}) are not in the logics "
244                             f"language of CHASE (contract {self.name})")
245        lines = [f"CONTRACT {self.name}:"]
246        for k, v in self.variables.items():
247            kind = "input" if k in self.inputs else "output"
248            typ = {"bool": "boolean", "real": "real"}.get(v) or f"integer ({v[0]}:{v[1]})"
249            lines.append(f"    {kind} {typ} variable {k};")
250        lines.append("    Assumptions:")
251        lines += [f"        {ltl.to_chase(f)};" for f in self.assumptions] or ["        true;"]
252        lines.append("    Guarantees:")
253        lines += [f"        {ltl.to_chase(f)};" for f in self.guarantees] or ["        true;"]
254        return "\n".join(lines) + "\n"
255
256    def to_pychase(self):
257        """Parse the contract with the CHASE core library and return the
258        pychase ``Contract`` (the CHASE objects are never freed)."""
259        return _parse_contracts([self])[self.name]
260
261    # Signature ---------------------------------------------------------------
262
263    def rename(self, mapping: Mapping[str, str], name: str | None = None) -> "Contract":
264        """The same contract with the variables renamed (old name -> new name)."""
265        def ren(node):
266            if isinstance(node, ltl.Var):
267                return ltl.Var(mapping.get(node.name, node.name), node.primed)
268            if isinstance(node, ltl.Unary):
269                return ltl.Unary(node.op, ren(node.arg))
270            if isinstance(node, ltl.Binary):
271                return ltl.Binary(node.op, ren(node.left), ren(node.right))
272            return node
273        c = Contract(name or self.name,
274                     {mapping.get(k, k): v for k, v in self.inputs.items()},
275                     {mapping.get(k, k): v for k, v in self.outputs.items()},
276                     [ren(f) for f in self.assumptions], [ren(f) for f in self.guarantees])
277        c.validate()
278        return c
279
280    def shares_io_with(self, other: "Contract") -> bool:
281        """Same inputs and outputs, with the same types."""
282        return self.inputs == other.inputs and self.outputs == other.outputs
283
284    def can_compose_with(self, other: "Contract") -> bool:
285        """No variable is an output of both contracts, and the shared
286        variables have the same type."""
287        if set(self.outputs) & set(other.outputs):
288            return False
289        return all(self.variables[v] == other.variables[v]
290                   for v in set(self.variables) & set(other.variables))
291
292    # Contract algebra (computed by the CHASE core library) -------------------
293
294    def simplify(self, name: str | None = None, nots: bool = True,
295                 temporal_operators: bool = True) -> "Contract":
296        """The contract with its formulas simplified by the core library (the
297        simplify command of logics_tool): the negations are moved towards the
298        atoms (nots), and the temporal operators are grouped
299        (temporal_operators): G f & G g becomes G (f & g), F f | F g becomes
300        F (f | g), X f & X g becomes X (f & g). The contract is equivalent."""
301        from ._native import utilities
302        abstraction = words.Abstraction()
303        holder = _parse_contracts([abstraction.contract(self)])
304        try:
305            pc = holder[self.name]
306            utilities.simplify(pc, utilities.simplify_options(nots, temporal_operators))
307            out = abstraction.restore(Contract.from_pychase(pc))
308        finally:
309            holder.free()
310        out.name = name or self.name
311        out.inputs = {v: t for v, t in out.variables.items() if v in self.inputs}
312        out.outputs = {v: t for v, t in out.variables.items() if v not in self.inputs}
313        return out
314
315    def saturate(self, name: str | None = None) -> "Contract":
316        """Saturation: the equivalent contract (A, A -> G)."""
317        guarantees = [self.saturated_guarantee] if self.assumptions else list(self.guarantees)
318        return Contract(name or self.name, dict(self.inputs), dict(self.outputs),
319                        list(self.assumptions), guarantees)
320
321    def compose(self, other: "Contract", name: str | None = None, discharge: bool = False,
322                backend: str = "auto", **options) -> "Contract":
323        """Parallel composition; variables with the same name are connected.
324
325        By default the closed form of the core library:
326        ((A1 & A2) | !(G1 & G2), G1 & G2).
327
328        With ``discharge=True``, the result keeps the terms of the two
329        contracts (Incer, PhD thesis 2022, Algorithm 2, without variable
330        elimination). When the outputs of one contract feed the inputs of the
331        other, each assumption of the receiving contract implied by the
332        assumptions and guarantees of the driving one is dropped; under
333        feedback, this is done in one direction only, the one that drops more
334        assumptions. Then the terms implied by the others are dropped as in
335        ``remove_redundant``. Each test is one implication check (nuXmv or
336        NuSMV; ``backend`` and ``options`` as for the checks). The result is
337        an abstraction of the composition: the closed form refines it, so a
338        refinement proved on it holds for the composition.
339        """
340        both = set(self.outputs) & set(other.outputs)
341        if both:
342            raise ValueError(f"cannot compose {self.name} and {other.name}: "
343                             f"{sorted(both)} are outputs of both")
344        name = name or f"{self.name}_{other.name}"
345        if discharge:
346            return _compose_terms(self, other, name, backend, **options)
347        return _algebra("composition", self, other, name)
348
349    def conjoin(self, other: "Contract", name: str | None = None, discharge: bool = False,
350                backend: str = "auto", **options) -> "Contract":
351        """Greatest lower bound (both specifications at once):
352        (A1 | A2, G1 & G2), with the contracts saturated.
353
354        With ``discharge=True``, the result keeps the terms of the two
355        contracts: each guarantee of one contract is guaranteed under the
356        assumptions of that contract that the other's do not imply (A1' -> g,
357        or g when there are none), and the assumption is A1 | A2, with the
358        terms implied by both sides taken out of the disjunction. When the
359        assumptions of one contract imply those of the other, the
360        disjunction goes away. This is the same contract as the
361        conjunction. Then the terms implied by the others are dropped as in
362        ``remove_redundant``. Each test is one implication check (nuXmv or
363        NuSMV; ``backend`` and ``options`` as for the checks).
364        """
365        name = name or f"{self.name}_and_{other.name}"
366        if discharge:
367            return _conjoin_terms(self, other, name, backend, **options)
368        return _algebra("conjunction", self, other, name)
369
370    def disjoin(self, other: "Contract", name: str | None = None) -> "Contract":
371        """Least upper bound: (A1 & A2, G1 | G2)."""
372        return _algebra("disjunction", self, other, name or f"{self.name}_or_{other.name}")
373
374    def merge(self, other: "Contract", name: str | None = None, discharge: bool = False,
375              backend: str = "auto", **options) -> "Contract":
376        """Merging of two viewpoints of the same component:
377        (A1 & A2, (G1 & G2) | !(A1 & A2)).
378
379        With ``discharge=True``, the result keeps the terms of the two
380        contracts: (A1 & A2, G1 & G2), whose saturation is the merge, so the
381        two are the same contract. Then the terms implied by the others are
382        dropped as in ``remove_redundant`` (one implication check each, with
383        nuXmv or NuSMV; ``backend`` and ``options`` as for the checks).
384        """
385        name = name or f"{self.name}_merge_{other.name}"
386        if discharge:
387            return _merge_terms(self, other, name, backend, **options)
388        return _algebra("merging", self, other, name)
389
390    def divide(self, other: "Contract", name: str | None = None, discharge: bool = False,
391               backend: str = "auto", **options) -> "Contract":
392        """Largest C such that other || C refines self:
393        (A1 & G2, (G1 & A2) | !(A1 & G2)), with the contracts saturated
394        (Incer et al., MEMOCODE 2018).
395
396        With ``discharge=True``, the result keeps the terms of the two
397        contracts: the assumptions are those of self and, for each guarantee
398        g of other, A2 -> g; the guarantees are those of self and the
399        assumptions of other. The assumptions of other implied by those of
400        self are discharged first: when all of them are, the guarantees of
401        other are kept as they are. This is the same contract as the
402        quotient. Then the terms implied by the others are dropped as in
403        ``remove_redundant``. Each test is one implication check (nuXmv or
404        NuSMV; ``backend`` and ``options`` as for the checks).
405        """
406        name = name or f"{self.name}_div_{other.name}"
407        if discharge:
408            return _divide_terms(self, other, name, backend, **options)
409        return _algebra("quotient", self, other, name)
410
411    def separate(self, other: "Contract", name: str | None = None) -> "Contract":
412        """Smallest C such that self refines other . C (merging):
413        ((A1 & G2) | !(G1 & A2), G1 & A2) (Passerone et al., TECS 2019)."""
414        return _algebra("separation", self, other, name or f"{self.name}_sep_{other.name}")
415
416    def imply(self, other: "Contract", name: str | None = None) -> "Contract":
417        """Implication self -> other, the adjoint of conjunction: the largest C
418        such that C conjoined with self refines other:
419        ((A2 & !A1) | (G1 & !G2), G2 | !G1) (Incer et al., arXiv 2309.08875,
420        Proposition 6)."""
421        return _algebra("implication", self, other, name or f"{self.name}_imply_{other.name}")
422
423    def coimply(self, other: "Contract", name: str | None = None) -> "Contract":
424        """Coimplication, the adjoint of disjunction: the smallest C such that
425        other refines C disjoined with self:
426        (A2 | !A1, (G2 & !G1) | (A1 & !A2)) (Incer et al., arXiv 2309.08875,
427        Proposition 7)."""
428        return _algebra("coimplication", self, other,
429                        name or f"{self.name}_coimply_{other.name}")
430
431    def invert(self, name: str | None = None) -> "Contract":
432        """Reciprocal (G, A): the contract seen from its environment; the
433        inputs become outputs and the outputs inputs."""
434        from ._native import representation as R
435        c = self.saturate()
436        abstraction = words.Abstraction()
437        holder = _parse_contracts([abstraction.contract(c)])
438        try:
439            result = R.Contract.reciprocal(holder[c.name], name or f"{self.name}_inv")
440            holder.results.append(result)
441            out = abstraction.restore(Contract.from_pychase(result))
442        finally:
443            holder.free()
444        variables = {**out.inputs, **out.outputs}
445        out.inputs = {v: t for v, t in variables.items() if v in self.outputs}
446        out.outputs = {v: t for v, t in variables.items() if v not in self.outputs}
447        return out
448
449    def assume(self, formula, name: str | None = None) -> "Contract":
450        """Adds the assumption b: (b & A, b -> G), the left action of Incer et
451        al., arXiv 2309.08875, Section 4, computed as the merging of (b, true)
452        with the contract. The result is an abstraction of the contract."""
453        b = _single_term(self, formula, assumption=True)
454        return _algebra("merging", self, b, name or f"{self.name}_assume")
455
456    def ensure(self, formula, name: str | None = None) -> "Contract":
457        """Adds the guarantee b: (b -> A, b & G), the right action of Incer et
458        al., arXiv 2309.08875, Section 4, computed as the composition of
459        (true, b) with the contract. The result refines the contract."""
460        b = _single_term(self, formula, assumption=False)
461        if not self.assumptions:        # (true, G) composed with (true, b) is (true, G & b): keep the terms
462            return Contract(name or f"{self.name}_ensure", dict(self.inputs), dict(self.outputs),
463                            [], list(self.guarantees) + list(b.guarantees))
464        return _algebra("composition", self, b, name or f"{self.name}_ensure")

An assume-guarantee contract.

assumptions and guarantees are lists of LTL formulas, read as conjunctions. Variables are Boolean ("bool"), bounded integers (low, high), or reals ("real").

def from_strings( cls, inputs=None, outputs=None, assumptions=None, guarantees=None, name: str = 'C') -> Contract: 
 89    @classmethod
 90    def from_strings(cls, inputs=None, outputs=None, assumptions=None,
 91                     guarantees=None, name: str = "C") -> "Contract":
 92        """Build a contract from formulas in the standard LTL syntax.
 93
 94        >>> c = Contract.from_strings(inputs=["req"], outputs=["grant"],
 95        ...                           assumptions=["G F !req"],
 96        ...                           guarantees=["G (req -> F grant)"])
 97        """
 98        c = cls(name=name, inputs=_normalize_vars(inputs),
 99                outputs=_normalize_vars(outputs),

101                guarantees=_normalize_formulas(guarantees))
102        c.validate()
103        return c

@classmethod
def from_pychase(cls, pc, shared=()) -> Contract: 
105    @classmethod
106    def from_pychase(cls, pc, shared=()) -> "Contract":
107        """Convert a contract of the CHASE core library. ``shared`` are the
108        declarations of the system (outside the contracts) that the contract
109        may use."""
110        from ._native import representation as R
111        inputs, outputs, generic, constants = {}, {}, {}, {}
112        for d in list(shared) + list(pc.declarations):
113            name = d.getName().getString()
114            t = d.getType()
115            kind = type(t).__name__
116            if kind not in ("Integer", "Boolean", "Real"):
117                raise ValueError(f"{name!r} has the type {kind}: only Boolean, integer, "
118                                 "and real variables are supported")
119            if type(d).__name__ == "Constant":
120                constants[name] = ltl.number(d.getValue().getValue())
121                continue
122            # A real without a range has the bounds -+infinity of the core library
123            # (the largest int64).
124            if kind == "Real" and (t.getMin() > -_UNBOUNDED or t.getMax() < _UNBOUNDED):
125                raise ValueError(f"{name!r} is a real with a range: write the range as an "
126                                 "assumption or a guarantee instead")
127            if kind == "Integer":
128                vtype = (t.getMin(), t.getMax())
129            else:
130                vtype = "real" if kind == "Real" else "bool"
131            causality = d.getCausality()
132            if causality == R.causality_t.input:
133                inputs[name] = vtype
134            elif causality == R.causality_t.generic:   # e.g. a proposition, inlined
135                generic[name] = vtype
136            else:
137                outputs[name] = vtype
138
139        def value(node):    # constants are replaced by their values
140            if isinstance(node, ltl.Var) and node.name in constants:
141                return ltl.Num(constants[node.name])
142            if isinstance(node, ltl.Unary):
143                return ltl.Unary(node.op, value(node.arg))
144            if isinstance(node, ltl.Binary):
145                return ltl.Binary(node.op, value(node.left), value(node.right))
146            return node
147
148        def terms(domain_map) -> list[ltl.Node]:
149            out = []
150            for domain, spec in domain_map.items():
151                # the formulas only: the DSL also puts its architecture there, as a graph
152                if type(spec).__name__ == "Graph":
153                    continue
154                out.extend(value(t) for t in ltl.conjuncts(ltl.from_pychase(spec)))
155            return out
156
157        assumptions, guarantees = terms(pc.assumptions), terms(pc.guarantees)
158        used = ltl.variables(ltl.conjunction(assumptions + guarantees))
159        outputs.update({k: v for k, v in generic.items() if k in used})
160        return cls(name=pc.getName().getString(), inputs=inputs, outputs=outputs,
161                   assumptions=assumptions, guarantees=guarantees)

Convert a contract of the CHASE core library. shared are the declarations of the system (outside the contracts) that the contract may use.

def validate(self) -> None: 
163    def validate(self) -> None:
164        for n in [self.name] + list(self.variables):
165            if n in RESERVED or not n.replace("_", "a").isalnum() or not n[0].isalpha():
166                raise ValueError(f"{n!r} cannot be used as a name: names start with a "
167                                 "letter, contain letters, digits and _, and are not "
168                                 f"keywords of CHASE ({', '.join(sorted(RESERVED))})")
169        both = set(self.inputs) & set(self.outputs)
170        if both:
171            raise ValueError(f"variables both input and output: {sorted(both)}")
172        declared = self.variables
173        for f in self.assumptions + self.guarantees:
174            missing = ltl.variables(f) - set(declared)
175            if missing:
176                raise ValueError(f"undeclared variables {sorted(missing)} in "
177                                 f"{ltl.to_str(f)!r} (contract {self.name})")
178        if words.has_words(declared):
179            for f in self.assumptions + self.guarantees:
180                try:
181                    words.check(f, declared)
182                except words.WordTypeError as e:
183                    raise ValueError(f"{e} (in {ltl.to_str(f)!r}, contract {self.name})") \
184                        from None

202        """A -> G."""
203        if not self.assumptions:
204            return self.guarantee
205        return ltl.Binary("->", self.assumption, self.guarantee)

def to_logics(self) -> str: 
239    def to_logics(self) -> str:
240        """The contract in the logics language of CHASE (as read by logics_tool)."""
241        found = sorted(v for v, t in self.variables.items() if words.word_type(t))
242        if found:
243            raise ValueError(f"word variables ({', '.join(found)}) are not in the logics "
244                             f"language of CHASE (contract {self.name})")
245        lines = [f"CONTRACT {self.name}:"]
246        for k, v in self.variables.items():
247            kind = "input" if k in self.inputs else "output"
248            typ = {"bool": "boolean", "real": "real"}.get(v) or f"integer ({v[0]}:{v[1]})"
249            lines.append(f"    {kind} {typ} variable {k};")
250        lines.append("    Assumptions:")
251        lines += [f"        {ltl.to_chase(f)};" for f in self.assumptions] or ["        true;"]
252        lines.append("    Guarantees:")
253        lines += [f"        {ltl.to_chase(f)};" for f in self.guarantees] or ["        true;"]
254        return "\n".join(lines) + "\n"

def rename( self, mapping: Mapping[str, str], name: str | None = None) -> Contract: 
263    def rename(self, mapping: Mapping[str, str], name: str | None = None) -> "Contract":
264        """The same contract with the variables renamed (old name -> new name)."""
265        def ren(node):
266            if isinstance(node, ltl.Var):
267                return ltl.Var(mapping.get(node.name, node.name), node.primed)
268            if isinstance(node, ltl.Unary):
269                return ltl.Unary(node.op, ren(node.arg))
270            if isinstance(node, ltl.Binary):
271                return ltl.Binary(node.op, ren(node.left), ren(node.right))
272            return node
273        c = Contract(name or self.name,
274                     {mapping.get(k, k): v for k, v in self.inputs.items()},
275                     {mapping.get(k, k): v for k, v in self.outputs.items()},
276                     [ren(f) for f in self.assumptions], [ren(f) for f in self.guarantees])
277        c.validate()
278        return c

The same contract with the variables renamed (old name -> new name).

286        variables have the same type."""

def simplify( self, name: str | None = None, nots: bool = True, temporal_operators: bool = True) -> Contract: 
294    def simplify(self, name: str | None = None, nots: bool = True,
295                 temporal_operators: bool = True) -> "Contract":
296        """The contract with its formulas simplified by the core library (the
297        simplify command of logics_tool): the negations are moved towards the
298        atoms (nots), and the temporal operators are grouped
299        (temporal_operators): G f & G g becomes G (f & g), F f | F g becomes
300        F (f | g), X f & X g becomes X (f & g). The contract is equivalent."""
301        from ._native import utilities
302        abstraction = words.Abstraction()
303        holder = _parse_contracts([abstraction.contract(self)])
304        try:
305            pc = holder[self.name]
306            utilities.simplify(pc, utilities.simplify_options(nots, temporal_operators))
307            out = abstraction.restore(Contract.from_pychase(pc))
308        finally:
309            holder.free()
310        out.name = name or self.name
311        out.inputs = {v: t for v, t in out.variables.items() if v in self.inputs}
312        out.outputs = {v: t for v, t in out.variables.items() if v not in self.inputs}
313        return out

The contract is equivalent.

def compose( self, other: Contract, name: str | None = None, discharge: bool = False, backend: str = 'auto', **options) -> Contract: 
321    def compose(self, other: "Contract", name: str | None = None, discharge: bool = False,
322                backend: str = "auto", **options) -> "Contract":
323        """Parallel composition; variables with the same name are connected.
324
325        By default the closed form of the core library:
326        ((A1 & A2) | !(G1 & G2), G1 & G2).
327
328        With ``discharge=True``, the result keeps the terms of the two
329        contracts (Incer, PhD thesis 2022, Algorithm 2, without variable
330        elimination). When the outputs of one contract feed the inputs of the
331        other, each assumption of the receiving contract implied by the
332        assumptions and guarantees of the driving one is dropped; under
333        feedback, this is done in one direction only, the one that drops more
334        assumptions. Then the terms implied by the others are dropped as in
335        ``remove_redundant``. Each test is one implication check (nuXmv or
336        NuSMV; ``backend`` and ``options`` as for the checks). The result is
337        an abstraction of the composition: the closed form refines it, so a
338        refinement proved on it holds for the composition.
339        """
340        both = set(self.outputs) & set(other.outputs)
341        if both:
342            raise ValueError(f"cannot compose {self.name} and {other.name}: "
343                             f"{sorted(both)} are outputs of both")
344        name = name or f"{self.name}_{other.name}"
345        if discharge:
346            return _compose_terms(self, other, name, backend, **options)
347        return _algebra("composition", self, other, name)

350                backend: str = "auto", **options) -> "Contract":

355        contracts: each guarantee of one contract is guaranteed under the
356        assumptions of that contract that the other's do not imply (A1' -> g,

358        terms implied by both sides taken out of the disjunction. When the

366        if discharge:
367            return _conjoin_terms(self, other, name, backend, **options)
368        return _algebra("conjunction", self, other, name)

398        g of other, A2 -> g; the guarantees are those of self and the
399        assumptions of other. The assumptions of other implied by those of
400        self are discharged first: when all of them are, the guarantees of
401        other are kept as they are. This is the same contract as the
402        quotient. Then the terms implied by the others are dropped as in
403        ``remove_redundant``. Each test is one implication check (nuXmv or
404        NuSMV; ``backend`` and ``options`` as for the checks).
405        """
406        name = name or f"{self.name}_div_{other.name}"
407        if discharge:
408            return _divide_terms(self, other, name, backend, **options)
409        return _algebra("quotient", self, other, name)

Largest C such that other || C refines self: (A1 & G2, (G1 & A2) | !(A1 & G2)), with the contracts saturated (Incer et al., MEMOCODE 2018).

With discharge=True, the result keeps the terms of the two contracts: the assumptions are those of self and, for each guarantee g of other, A2 -> g; the guarantees are those of self and the assumptions of other. The assumptions of other implied by those of self are discharged first: when all of them are, the guarantees of other are kept as they are. This is the same contract as the quotient. Then the terms implied by the others are dropped as in remove_redundant. Each test is one implication check (nuXmv or NuSMV; backend and options as for the checks).

def separate( self, other: Contract, name: str | None = None) -> Contract: 
411    def separate(self, other: "Contract", name: str | None = None) -> "Contract":
412        """Smallest C such that self refines other . C (merging):
413        ((A1 & G2) | !(G1 & A2), G1 & A2) (Passerone et al., TECS 2019)."""
414        return _algebra("separation", self, other, name or f"{self.name}_sep_{other.name}")

Smallest C such that self refines other . C (merging): ((A1 & G2) | !(G1 & A2), G1 & A2) (Passerone et al., TECS 2019).

def imply( self, other: Contract, name: str | None = None) -> Contract: 
416    def imply(self, other: "Contract", name: str | None = None) -> "Contract":
417        """Implication self -> other, the adjoint of conjunction: the largest C
418        such that C conjoined with self refines other:
419        ((A2 & !A1) | (G1 & !G2), G2 | !G1) (Incer et al., arXiv 2309.08875,
420        Proposition 6)."""
421        return _algebra("implication", self, other, name or f"{self.name}_imply_{other.name}")

Implication self -> other, the adjoint of conjunction: the largest C such that C conjoined with self refines other: ((A2 & !A1) | (G1 & !G2), G2 | !G1) (Incer et al., arXiv 2309.08875, Proposition 6).

def coimply( self, other: Contract, name: str | None = None) -> Contract: 
423    def coimply(self, other: "Contract", name: str | None = None) -> "Contract":
424        """Coimplication, the adjoint of disjunction: the smallest C such that
425        other refines C disjoined with self:
426        (A2 | !A1, (G2 & !G1) | (A1 & !A2)) (Incer et al., arXiv 2309.08875,
427        Proposition 7)."""
428        return _algebra("coimplication", self, other,
429                        name or f"{self.name}_coimply_{other.name}")

Coimplication, the adjoint of disjunction: the smallest C such that other refines C disjoined with self: (A2 | !A1, (G2 & !G1) | (A1 & !A2)) (Incer et al., arXiv 2309.08875, Proposition 7).

def invert(self, name: str | None = None) -> Contract: 
431    def invert(self, name: str | None = None) -> "Contract":
432        """Reciprocal (G, A): the contract seen from its environment; the
433        inputs become outputs and the outputs inputs."""
434        from ._native import representation as R
435        c = self.saturate()
436        abstraction = words.Abstraction()
437        holder = _parse_contracts([abstraction.contract(c)])
438        try:
439            result = R.Contract.reciprocal(holder[c.name], name or f"{self.name}_inv")
440            holder.results.append(result)
441            out = abstraction.restore(Contract.from_pychase(result))
442        finally:
443            holder.free()
444        variables = {**out.inputs, **out.outputs}
445        out.inputs = {v: t for v, t in variables.items() if v in self.outputs}
446        out.outputs = {v: t for v, t in variables.items() if v not in self.outputs}
447        return out

Reciprocal (G, A): the contract seen from its environment; the inputs become outputs and the outputs inputs.

def assume(self, formula, name: str | None = None) -> Contract: 
449    def assume(self, formula, name: str | None = None) -> "Contract":
450        """Adds the assumption b: (b & A, b -> G), the left action of Incer et
451        al., arXiv 2309.08875, Section 4, computed as the merging of (b, true)
452        with the contract. The result is an abstraction of the contract."""
453        b = _single_term(self, formula, assumption=True)
454        return _algebra("merging", self, b, name or f"{self.name}_assume")

Adds the assumption b: (b & A, b -> G), the left action of Incer et al., arXiv 2309.08875, Section 4, computed as the merging of (b, true) with the contract. The result is an abstraction of the contract.

def ensure(self, formula, name: str | None = None) -> Contract: 
456    def ensure(self, formula, name: str | None = None) -> "Contract":
457        """Adds the guarantee b: (b -> A, b & G), the right action of Incer et
458        al., arXiv 2309.08875, Section 4, computed as the composition of
459        (true, b) with the contract. The result refines the contract."""
460        b = _single_term(self, formula, assumption=False)
461        if not self.assumptions:        # (true, G) composed with (true, b) is (true, G & b): keep the terms
462            return Contract(name or f"{self.name}_ensure", dict(self.inputs), dict(self.outputs),
463                            [], list(self.guarantees) + list(b.guarantees))
464        return _algebra("composition", self, b, name or f"{self.name}_ensure")

Adds the guarantee b: (b -> A, b & G), the right action of Incer et al., arXiv 2309.08875, Section 4, computed as the composition of (true, b) with the contract. The result refines the contract.

def load_dsl( path: str | os.PathLike, name: str | None = None) -> Contract: 
674def load_dsl(path: str | os.PathLike, name: str | None = None) -> Contract:
675    """The contract of a problem written in the domain-specific language of
676    CHASE (dsl_tool: components, connections, and patterns of requirements),
677    with the formulas the patterns give. The architecture, a graph, is left
678    out. The contract is named ``name``, or after the file."""
679    if not os.path.isfile(path):
680        raise FileNotFoundError(f"no such file: {os.fspath(path)}")
681    from ._native import _load
682    builder = _load("pychase_DSL").DSLSpecsBuilder()
683    builder.parseSpecificationFile(os.fspath(path))
684    c = Contract.from_pychase(builder.getContract())
685    c.name = name or os.path.splitext(os.path.basename(os.fspath(path)))[0]
686    return c

The contract of a problem written in the domain-specific language of CHASE (dsl_tool: components, connections, and patterns of requirements), with the formulas the patterns give. The architecture, a graph, is left out. The contract is named name, or after the file.

def load_spec( path: str | os.PathLike, _name: str | None = None) -> dict[str, Contract]: 
689def load_spec(path: str | os.PathLike, _name: str | None = None) -> dict[str, Contract]:
690    """The contracts of a specification file in the logics language of CHASE,
691    by name."""
692    if not os.path.isfile(path):
693        raise FileNotFoundError(f"no such file: {os.fspath(path)}")
694    from ._native import utilities
695    system = _parse_file(os.fspath(path), _name or os.fspath(path))
696    try:
697        contracts = {c.getName().getString(): c for c in system.getContractsSet()}
698        shared = list(system.getDeclarationsSet())
699        out = {}
700        for name in sorted(contracts):
701            try:
702                c = Contract.from_pychase(contracts[name], shared)
703            except ValueError as e:              # which contract, in the message
704                raise ValueError(f"contract {name}: {e}") from None
705            # keep the shared declarations the contract uses
706            used = ltl.variables(ltl.conjunction(c.assumptions + c.guarantees))
707            local = {d.getName().getString() for d in contracts[name].declarations}
708            c.inputs = {v: t for v, t in c.inputs.items() if v in used or v in local}
709            c.outputs = {v: t for v, t in c.outputs.items() if v in used or v in local}
710            out[name] = c
711    finally:
712        utilities.destroy(system)
713    for c in out.values():
714        _warn_outside_ranges(c, _name or os.fspath(path))
715    return out

The contracts of a specification file in the logics language of CHASE, by name.

def parse_sva( text: str, inputs=None, outputs=None, name: str | None = None, parameters: dict | None = None, clock: str | None = None) -> SVAReading: 
2493def parse_sva(text: str, inputs=None, outputs=None, name: Optional[str] = None,
2494              parameters: Optional[dict] = None, clock: Optional[str] = None) -> SVAReading:
2495    """Read the assumptions and assertions of SVA text as a contract.
2496
2497    ``inputs`` and ``outputs`` (lists of names, or dicts of types) say which
2498    signals the environment controls; for the other signals the directions
2499    of the module ports are used (the attribute ``(* chase = "output" *)``,
2500    written by ``to_sva``, overrides them), and the signals that are not
2501    ports are of the other kind than the list given. Hierarchical names
2502    (``u1.state``) are read as ``u1__state``; ``names`` of the result maps
2503    them back. Types: the declarations of the text, then
2504    the values of the dicts ("bool", "word[8]", "signed word[8]"), else
2505    Booleans. ``parameters`` gives the values of parameters (they override
2506    those of the text). ``assume property`` and ``restrict property`` give
2507    assumptions, ``assert property`` guarantees; ``cover property`` is kept
2508    apart (``covers``). A contract has one clock: ``clock`` ("posedge clk")
2509    chooses it when the text has several, else the clock of most properties
2510    is taken, and the properties of the other clocks are skipped. Signals
2511    without a declaration or a type are read as 1-bit signals and listed in
2512    ``undeclared``.
2513    """
2514    scan = _Scanner(text)
2515    scan.run()
2516    params = dict(scan.params)
2517    for k, v in (parameters or {}).items():
2518        params[k] = int(v)
2519    clocks = {c for c in [scan.default_clock] if c}
2520    main_clock = _main_clock(scan, clock)
2521    reading = SVAReading(Contract(name or scan.module or "C"), skipped=list(scan.notes))
2522    types = {k: v for k, v in scan.decls.items()}
2523    given = {}
2524    flat = lambda v: v.replace(".", "__")      # noqa: E731  hierarchical names
2525    inputs = {flat(v): t for v, t in inputs.items()} if isinstance(inputs, dict) else \
2526        [flat(v) for v in inputs] if inputs is not None else None
2527    outputs = {flat(v): t for v, t in outputs.items()} if isinstance(outputs, dict) else \
2528        [flat(v) for v in outputs] if outputs is not None else None
2529    for group, direction in ((inputs, "input"), (outputs, "output")):
2530        if isinstance(group, dict):
2531            for v, t in group.items():
2532                given[v] = direction
2533                if v not in types and t is not None:
2534                    types[v] = _decl_of(t)
2535        elif group:
2536            for v in group:
2537                given[v] = direction
2538
2539    vector_bits: set = set()
2540    while True:
2541        meaning = _Meaning(scan, params, dict(types), vector_bits)
2542        results, retry = _read_all(scan, meaning, clocks, main_clock)
2543        if retry is None:
2544            break
2545        vector_bits.add(retry)
2546    for kind, item in results:
2547        if kind == "skip":
2548            reading.skipped.append(item)
2549        elif kind == "cover":
2550            reading.covers.append(item)
2551        else:
2552            reading.properties.append(item)
2553    reading.clock = main_clock
2554    reading.names = {v: scan.p.names[v] for v in sorted(meaning.used) if v in scan.p.names}
2555    reading.undeclared = sorted(v for v in meaning.used if v not in meaning.declared)
2556
2557    used = sorted(meaning.used)
2558    variables = {}
2559    for v in used:
2560        dec = meaning.types[v]
2561        if dec.width == 1 and v not in vector_bits:
2562            variables[v] = "bool"
2563        else:
2564            variables[v] = f"{'signed ' if dec.signed else ''}word[{dec.width}]"
2565    # what is given, then the ports of the module, then the other kind of signal
2566    other = "output" if inputs is not None and outputs is None else \
2567        "input" if outputs is not None and inputs is None else None
2568    directions = {v: given.get(v) or meaning.types[v].direction or other for v in used}
2569    unknown = [v for v, dirn in directions.items() if dirn not in ("input", "output")]
2570    if unknown:
2571        raise SVAError(f"say whether these signals are inputs or outputs: {unknown} "
2572                       "(inputs=[...]; the other signals are outputs)")
2573    c = reading.contract
2574    c.inputs = {v: variables[v] for v in used if directions[v] == "input"}
2575    c.outputs = {v: variables[v] for v in used if directions[v] == "output"}
2576    c.assumptions = [p.formula for p in reading.properties if p.kind == "assume"]
2577    c.guarantees = [p.formula for p in reading.properties if p.kind == "assert"]
2578    c.validate()
2579    return reading

Read the assumptions and assertions of SVA text as a contract.

inputs and outputs (lists of names, or dicts of types) say which signals the environment controls; for the other signals the directions of the module ports are used (the attribute (* chase = "output" *), written by to_sva, overrides them), and the signals that are not ports are of the other kind than the list given. Hierarchical names (u1.state) are read as u1__state; names of the result maps them back. Types: the declarations of the text, then the values of the dicts ("bool", "word[8]", "signed word[8]"), else Booleans. parameters gives the values of parameters (they override those of the text). assume property and restrict property give assumptions, assert property guarantees; cover property is kept apart (covers). A contract has one clock: clock ("posedge clk") chooses it when the text has several, else the clock of most properties is taken, and the properties of the other clocks are skipped. Signals without a declaration or a type are read as 1-bit signals and listed in undeclared.

def to_sva( contract: Contract, clock: str = 'clk', edge: str = 'posedge', reset: str | None = None, module: str | None = None, bind: str | None = None, names: dict | None = None) -> str: 
2723def to_sva(contract: Contract, clock: str = "clk", edge: str = "posedge",
2724           reset: Optional[str] = None, module: Optional[str] = None,
2725           bind: Optional[str] = None, names: Optional[dict] = None) -> str:
2726    """The contract as a SystemVerilog checker module.
2727
2728    Assumptions become ``assume property``, guarantees ``assert property``,
2729    all clocked by ``@(edge clock)``; a formula G p is checked at every
2730    cycle, any other formula once, at the first cycle (``initial``).
2731    ``reset``, an expression such as "rst" or "!rst_n", disables the
2732    properties while it holds. Words are vectors (``logic [7:0]``), integer
2733    ranges ``int`` with their range assumed (inputs) or asserted (outputs).
2734    With ``bind``, the name of a design module, a bind statement puts the
2735    checker in every instance of it; its ports connect by name (``.*``).
2736    ``names`` gives the names of the signals in the design where they
2737    differ, such as the hierarchical names of ``parse_sva`` (its
2738    ``names``): the bind statement connects them. Real variables cannot be
2739    written.
2740    """
2741    module = module or f"{contract.name}_sva"
2742    variables = contract.variables
2743    bad = sorted(v for v in list(variables) + [clock, module] if v in SV_KEYWORDS)
2744    if bad:
2745        raise SVAError(f"names that are SystemVerilog keywords: {bad}")
2746    reals = sorted(v for v, t in variables.items() if t == "real")
2747    if reals:
2748        raise SVAError(f"real variables cannot be written in SVA: {reals}")
2749    w = _Writer(variables)
2750    lines = [f"// Contract {contract.name}, written by CHASE (chase_cps.to_sva).",
2751             f"// Assumptions: assume property; guarantees: assert property.",
2752             f"module {module} ("]
2753    ports = [f"  input logic {clock}"]
2754    if reset:
2755        for v in dict.fromkeys(re.findall(r"[A-Za-z_]\w*", reset)):
2756            if v not in variables and v != clock:
2757                ports.append(f"  input logic {v}")
2758    for group, role in ((contract.inputs, "input"), (contract.outputs, "output")):
2759        for v, t in group.items():
2760            ports.append(f'  (* chase = "{role}" *) input {_sv_type(t)} {v}')
2761    lines.append(",\n".join(ports))
2762    lines.append(");")
2763    event = f"@({edge} {clock})"
2764    disable = f" disable iff ({reset})" if reset else ""
2765
2766    def statement(kind, label, f):
2767        if isinstance(f, ltl.Unary) and f.op == "G":
2768            return f"  {label}: {kind} property ({event}{disable}\n    {w.prop(f.arg)});"
2769        return f"  initial {label}: {kind} property ({event}{disable}\n    {w.prop(f)});"
2770
2771    ranges = [(v, t, "assume" if v in contract.inputs else "assert")
2772              for v, t in variables.items() if isinstance(t, tuple)]
2773    if ranges:
2774        lines.append("  // integer ranges")
2775        for v, (lo, hi), kind in ranges:
2776            lines.append(f"  range_{v}: {kind} property ({event}{disable} "
2777                         f"{lo} <= {v} && {v} <= {hi});")
2778    if contract.assumptions:
2779        lines.append("  // assumptions")
2780        for i, f in enumerate(contract.assumptions):
2781            lines.append(statement("assume", f"A{i}", f))
2782    if contract.guarantees:
2783        lines.append("  // guarantees")
2784        for i, f in enumerate(contract.guarantees):
2785            lines.append(statement("assert", f"G{i}", f))
2786    lines.append("endmodule")
2787    if bind:
2788        extra = "".join(f", .{v}({n})" for v, n in sorted((names or {}).items())
2789                        if v in variables)
2790        lines += ["", f"bind {bind} {module} {module}_i (.*{extra});"]
2791    return "\n".join(lines) + "\n"

The contract as a SystemVerilog checker module.

Assumptions become assume property, guarantees assert property, all clocked by @(edge clock); a formula G p is checked at every cycle, any other formula once, at the first cycle (initial). reset, an expression such as "rst" or "!rst_n", disables the properties while it holds. Words are vectors (logic [7:0]), integer ranges int with their range assumed (inputs) or asserted (outputs). With bind, the name of a design module, a bind statement puts the checker in every instance of it; its ports connect by name (.*). names gives the names of the signals in the design where they differ, such as the hierarchical names of parse_sva (its names): the bind statement connects them. Real variables cannot be written.

def refines( refined: Contract, abstract: Contract, backend: str = 'auto', context=None, **options) -> RefinementResult: 
 89def refines(refined: Contract, abstract: Contract, backend: str = "auto",
 90            context=None, **options) -> RefinementResult:
 91    """Does ``refined`` refine ``abstract`` (can it replace it)?"""
 92    variables = _merge_vars(refined, abstract)
 93    a = implies(abstract.assumption, refined.assumption, variables, backend, context,
 94                **options)
 95    g = implies(refined.saturated_guarantee, abstract.saturated_guarantee, variables, backend,
 96                context, **options)
 97    if a.status == VALID and g.status == VALID:
 98        status = VALID
 99    elif INVALID in (a.status, g.status):
100        status = INVALID
101    else:
102        status = UNKNOWN
103    return RefinementResult(status, a, g)

Does refined refine abstract (can it replace it)?

def verify( contract: Contract, backend: str = 'auto', context=None, core: bool = False, **options) -> Verification: 
181def verify(contract: Contract, backend: str = "auto", context=None, core: bool = False,
182           **options) -> Verification:
183    """Can the assumptions and the guarantees of the contract hold together
184    (A & G satisfiable)? This implies that the contract is compatible and
185    consistent; when A & G is unsatisfiable, the two are checked to tell
186    whether the assumptions alone cannot hold. With core, an unsat result
187    carries ``unsat_core`` of the contract (the terms that conflict)."""
188    both = ltl.Binary("&", contract.assumption, contract.guarantee)
189    feasible = is_satisfiable(both, contract.variables, backend, context=context, **options)
190    if feasible.status == SAT:
191        def implied():
192            return replace(feasible, seconds=0.0, details={"implied by": "A & G"})
193        return Verification(implied(), implied(), feasible)
194    if core and feasible.status == UNSAT:
195        feasible.core = unsat_core(contract, backend=backend, context=context, **options)
196    return Verification(is_compatible(contract, backend, core=core, context=context, **options),
197                        is_consistent(contract, backend, core=core, context=context, **options),
198                        feasible)

Can the assumptions and the guarantees of the contract hold together (A & G satisfiable)? This implies that the contract is compatible and consistent; when A & G is unsatisfiable, the two are checked to tell whether the assumptions alone cannot hold. With core, an unsat result carries unsat_core of the contract (the terms that conflict).

def is_compatible( contract: Contract, backend: str = 'auto', core: bool = False, context=None, **options) -> Result: 
119def is_compatible(contract: Contract, backend: str = "auto", core: bool = False,
120                  context=None, **options) -> Result:
121    """Is there an environment allowed by the contract (A satisfiable)? With
122    core, an unsat result carries ``unsat_core`` of the assumptions."""
123    r = is_satisfiable(contract.assumption, contract.variables, backend, context=context,
124                       **options)
125    if core and r.status == UNSAT:
126        r.core = unsat_core(_only(contract, guarantees=False), backend=backend,
127                                  context=context, **options)
128    return r

Is there an environment allowed by the contract (A satisfiable)? With core, an unsat result carries unsat_core of the assumptions.

def is_consistent( contract: Contract, backend: str = 'auto', core: bool = False, context=None, **options) -> Result: 
106def is_consistent(contract: Contract, backend: str = "auto", core: bool = False,
107                  context=None, **options) -> Result:
108    """Is there a behavior allowed by the contract (A -> G satisfiable)? A -> G
109    is unsatisfiable only when A is valid and G unsatisfiable; with core, an
110    unsat result carries ``unsat_core`` of the guarantees."""
111    r = is_satisfiable(contract.saturated_guarantee, contract.variables, backend,
112                       context=context, **options)
113    if core and r.status == UNSAT:
114        r.core = unsat_core(_only(contract, guarantees=True), backend=backend,
115                                  context=context, **options)
116    return r

Is there a behavior allowed by the contract (A -> G satisfiable)? A -> G is unsatisfiable only when A is valid and G unsatisfiable; with core, an unsat result carries unsat_core of the guarantees.

def is_implementation( implementation, contract: Contract, backend: str = 'auto', context=None, **options) -> Result: 
334def is_implementation(implementation, contract: Contract, backend: str = "auto",
335                      context=None, **options) -> Result:
336    """Is M an implementation of the contract (M |=_M C), i.e. does M & A -> G
337    hold? The implementation is an LTL formula that describes the behaviors
338    of a component, or a state machine: a ``Model``, SMV text, a state
339    machine in JSON, or a controller of ``synthesize`` (see
340    ``chase_cps.models``), whose every behavior must satisfy A -> G. A
341    machine that refuses inputs can implement a contract only because of
342    that: ``is_receptive`` checks it."""
343    from .models import as_model
344    m = as_model(implementation, contract)
345    if m is None:
346        return implies(ltl.Binary("&", _formula(implementation), contract.assumption),
347                       contract.guarantee, contract.variables, backend, context, **options)
348    return _holds(m, contract.saturated_guarantee, contract, f"the contract {contract.name}",
349                  backend, context, **options)

Is M an implementation of the contract (M |=_M C), i.e. does M & A -> G hold? The implementation is an LTL formula that describes the behaviors of a component, or a state machine: a Model, SMV text, a state machine in JSON, or a controller of synthesize (see chase_cps.models), whose every behavior must satisfy A -> G. A machine that refuses inputs can implement a contract only because of that: is_receptive checks it.

331                  backend, context, **options)

def remove_redundant( contract: Contract, backend: str = 'auto', context=None, synth: bool = False, core: bool = False, **options) -> Redundancy: 
243def remove_redundant(contract: Contract, backend: str = "auto", context=None,
244                     synth: bool = False, core: bool = False, **options) -> Redundancy:
245    """Drop each term implied by the other terms and the context.
246
247    An assumption is dropped when the other assumptions imply it; a guarantee
248    when the assumptions and the other guarantees imply it. Each test is one
249    implication check, with the terms that share variables with the term
250    (see ``logic._Implications``); a term whose check does not finish is
251    kept. This keeps the contract, A -> G: use it before the algebra and the
252    checks (compose, refines, verify, is_implementation, ...).
253
254    With synth=True, a term is dropped only when it is implied in the GR(1)
255    game, which keeps realizability and the controllers: use it before
256    synthesis (is_realizable, synthesize, is_well_separated, is_vacuous,
257    unrealizable_core). The terms must be GR(1), and there is no context.
258    Each kind of term is implied only by some kinds of terms (see
259    ``chase_cps.gr1``): a safety guarantee is not dropped because a justice
260    assumption implies it, since the component must keep its safety
261    guarantees even when the environment breaks its justice assumptions.
262    The two differ only when the assumptions are wrong, for instance
263    unsatisfiable, or constrain the outputs; each keeps what the other may
264    change.
265
266    With core, each removed term carries a minimal set of the terms that
267    imply it.
268    """
269    c = contract
270    out = Redundancy(Contract(c.name, dict(c.inputs), dict(c.outputs),
271                                  list(c.assumptions), list(c.guarantees)))
272    if synth:
273        if context is not None:
274            raise TypeError("remove_redundant with synth=True does not take a context: "
275                            "the realizability checks read every behavior")
276        from .gr1 import _redundant_in_game
277        removed, out.unknown, out.reason, alive = _redundant_in_game(c, core, backend, **options)
278        out.removed = [RedundantTerm(t, part, kind, found) for part, t, kind, found in removed]
279        n = len(c.assumptions)
280        out.contract.assumptions = [t for j, t in enumerate(c.assumptions) if j in alive]
281        out.contract.guarantees = [t for j, t in enumerate(c.guarantees) if j + n in alive]
282        out.removed_assumptions = [t.term for t in out.removed if t.part == "assumption"]
283        out.removed_guarantees = [t.term for t in out.removed if t.part == "guarantee"]
284        return out
285    check = _Implications(list(c.assumptions) + list(c.guarantees), c.variables, backend,
286                          context, **options)
287
288    def drop(premises, term, part):
289        r = check(premises, term)
290        if r.status == UNKNOWN:
291            out.unknown.append(term)
292        if r.status != VALID:
293            return False
294        found = None
295        if core:
296            search = _Search(lambda idx: {VALID: True, INVALID: False}.get(
297                check([premises[k] for k in idx], term).status))
298            idx = search.ddmin(list(range(len(premises))), [])
299            found = None if search.reason else [premises[k] for k in idx]
300        out.removed.append(RedundantTerm(term, part, None, found))
301        return True
302
303    kept = list(c.assumptions)
304    for term in list(kept):
305        if drop([t for t in kept if t is not term], term, "assumption"):
306            kept.remove(term)
307            out.removed_assumptions.append(term)
308    out.contract.assumptions = kept
309    kept_g = list(c.guarantees)
310    for term in list(kept_g):
311        if drop(kept + [t for t in kept_g if t is not term], term, "guarantee"):
312            kept_g.remove(term)
313            out.removed_guarantees.append(term)
314    out.contract.guarantees = kept_g
315    return out

Drop each term implied by the other terms and the context.

An assumption is dropped when the other assumptions imply it; a guarantee when the assumptions and the other guarantees imply it. Each test is one implication check, with the terms that share variables with the term (see logic._Implications); a term whose check does not finish is kept. This keeps the contract, A -> G: use it before the algebra and the checks (compose, refines, verify, is_implementation, ...).

With synth=True, a term is dropped only when it is implied in the GR(1) game, which keeps realizability and the controllers: use it before synthesis (is_realizable, synthesize, is_well_separated, is_vacuous, unrealizable_core). The terms must be GR(1), and there is no context. Each kind of term is implied only by some kinds of terms (see chase_cps.gr1): a safety guarantee is not dropped because a justice assumption implies it, since the component must keep its safety guarantees even when the environment breaks its justice assumptions. The two differ only when the assumptions are wrong, for instance unsatisfiable, or constrain the outputs; each keeps what the other may change.

With core, each removed term carries a minimal set of the terms that imply it.

138@dataclass
139class Verification:
140    """Outcome of ``verify``. The status is that of ``feasible``: some
141    behavior satisfies A & G, so the assumptions and the guarantees can hold
142    together. ``compatible`` (A satisfiable) and ``consistent`` (A -> G
143    satisfiable) follow from it, with the same witness; when A & G is
144    unsatisfiable they say whether the assumptions alone cannot hold."""
145    compatible: Result
146    consistent: Result
147    feasible: Optional[Result] = None
148
149    @property
150    def status(self) -> str:
151        if self.feasible is not None:
152            return self.feasible.status
153        statuses = {self.compatible.status, self.consistent.status}
154        if statuses == {SAT}:
155            return SAT
156        return UNSAT if UNSAT in statuses else UNKNOWN
157
158    def __bool__(self) -> bool:
159        return self.status == SAT
160
161    @property
162    def seconds(self) -> float:
163        return sum(r.seconds for r in (self.feasible, self.compatible, self.consistent) if r)
164
165    @property
166    def reals(self) -> str | None:
167        """How the real variables were handled (see ``Result.reals``)."""
168        return _reals(*(r for r in (self.feasible, self.compatible, self.consistent) if r))
169
170    def to_dict(self) -> dict:
171        d = {"status": self.status}
172        if self.feasible is not None:
173            d["feasible"] = self.feasible.to_dict()
174        d["compatible"] = self.compatible.to_dict()
175        d["consistent"] = self.consistent.to_dict()
176        if self.reals:
177            d["reals"] = self.reals
178        return d

@dataclass
class Model: 
112@dataclass
113class Model:
114    """A state machine as an SMV program (MODULE main, no specification).
115    ``variables`` are the variables it declares (VAR, IVAR, FROZENVAR) and
116    defines (DEFINE), with their types; ``ivars`` the ones declared IVAR."""
117    name: str
118    smv: str
119    variables: dict[str, VarType] = field(default_factory=dict)
120    ivars: set[str] = field(default_factory=set)
121    start: int = 0      # the steps of a reset: the contracts are checked after them
122    # Where the model comes from (RTL files, a controller), for the diagrams
123    # (chase_cps.explicit); not used by the checks.
124    source: Optional[dict] = field(default=None, compare=False, repr=False)
125
126    @classmethod
127    def from_smv(cls, source: str, name: Optional[str] = None) -> "Model":
128        """A model from SMV text or the path of an SMV file. The module main
129        holds the variables of the contracts it is checked against; it must
130        not have specifications (LTLSPEC, SPEC, ...)."""
131        text = source
132        if "MODULE" not in source and os.path.exists(source):
133            with open(source) as f:
134                text = f.read()
135            name = name or os.path.splitext(os.path.basename(source))[0]
136        variables, ivars = {}, set()
137        for kw, start, stop in _sections(text):
138            if kw in _SPECS:
139                raise ValueError(f"the SMV model has a specification ({kw}): CHASE adds the "
140                                 "specification of each check")
141            if kw in ("VAR", "IVAR", "FROZENVAR"):
142                for m in _DECL.finditer(_strip_comments(text)[start:stop]):
143                    variables[m.group(1)] = _vartype(m.group(2))
144                    if kw == "IVAR":
145                        ivars.add(m.group(1))
146            elif kw == "DEFINE":
147                for m in re.finditer(r"([A-Za-z_][\w$#-]*)\s*:=", _strip_comments(text)[start:stop]):
148                    variables.setdefault(m.group(1), "define")
149        model = cls(name or "M", text, variables, ivars)
150        model.source = {"kind": "smv"}
151        return model
152
153    @classmethod
154    def from_rtl(cls, files, top: str, **options) -> "Model":
155        """The module ``top`` of Verilog or SystemVerilog files, read with
156        Yosys (see ``chase_cps.rtl.from_rtl`` for the options)."""
157        from .rtl import from_rtl
158        return from_rtl(files, top, **options)
159
160    @classmethod
161    def from_dict(cls, d: dict) -> "Model":
162        """A model from a state machine in JSON::
163
164            {"name": "Arbiter",
165             "inputs": {"req": "bool"}, "outputs": {"grant": "bool"},
166             "states": ["idle", "busy"], "initial": "idle",
167             "transitions": [
168               {"from": "idle", "when": "req", "outputs": {"grant": true}, "to": "busy"},
169               {"from": "idle", "when": "!req", "outputs": {"grant": false}, "to": "idle"},
170               {"from": "busy", "outputs": {"grant": false}, "to": "idle"}]}
171
172        At each step the environment sets the inputs; in its state, the
173        machine takes a transition whose ``when`` (a formula over the inputs
174        and the outputs, true when absent) holds, sets the outputs of the
175        same step as ``outputs`` says (an output not given is free), and
176        moves to ``to`` for the next step. ``initial`` is a state or a list
177        of states. The types are those of ``Contract.from_dict``: "bool",
178        or [min, max] for an integer range. With no transition to take, the
179        machine refuses the input (see ``is_receptive``).
180        """
181        name = d.get("name", "M")
182        inputs = {k: tuple(v) if isinstance(v, list) else v for k, v in d.get("inputs", {}).items()}
183        outputs = {k: tuple(v) if isinstance(v, list) else v
184                   for k, v in d.get("outputs", {}).items()}
185        states = list(d.get("states", []))
186        for s in states:
187            if not _NAME.match(s) or s in ("TRUE", "FALSE"):
188                raise ValueError(f"state {s!r}: the states must be identifiers")
189        if not states:
190            raise ValueError("the state machine has no states")
191        initial = d.get("initial", states[0])
192        initial = [initial] if isinstance(initial, str) else list(initial)
193        for s in initial:
194            if s not in states:
195                raise ValueError(f"the initial state {s!r} is not a state")
196        variables = {**inputs, **outputs}
197        cases = []
198        for i, t in enumerate(d.get("transitions", [])):
199            src, dst = t.get("from"), t.get("to")
200            if src not in states or dst not in states:
201                raise ValueError(f"transition {i}: from and to must be states")
202            parts = [f"chase_state = {src}"]
203            if t.get("when") not in (None, "", "true"):
204                when = ltl.parse(t["when"]) if isinstance(t["when"], str) else t["when"]
205                bad = ltl.variables(when) - set(variables)
206                if bad:
207                    raise ValueError(f"transition {i}: undeclared variables {sorted(bad)}")
208                if _has_temporal(when):
209                    raise ValueError(f"transition {i}: when must not have temporal operators")
210                parts.append(words.to_smv(when, variables))
211            for o, v in t.get("outputs", {}).items():
212                if o not in outputs:
213                    raise ValueError(f"transition {i}: {o} is not an output")
214                parts.append(f"{o} = {_smv_value(v, variables.get(o))}")
215            parts.append(f"next(chase_state) = {dst}")
216            cases.append("(" + " & ".join(parts) + ")")
217        lines = ["MODULE main", "VAR", f"    chase_state : {{{', '.join(states)}}};"]
218        lines += [f"    {v} : {_smvtype(t)};" for v, t in variables.items()]
219        lines.append("INIT " + " | ".join(f"chase_state = {s}" for s in initial) + ";")
220        lines.append("TRANS " + (" | ".join(cases) if cases else "FALSE") + ";")
221        model = cls(name, "\n".join(lines) + "\n", dict(variables), set())
222        model.variables["chase_state"] = "{" + ", ".join(states) + "}"
223        model.source = {"kind": "json", "dict": d}
224        return model
225
226    @classmethod
227    def from_controller(cls, controller, contract: Optional[Contract] = None,
228                        name: Optional[str] = None) -> "Model":
229        """The model of a controller synthesized by slugs: the result of
230        ``synthesize``, or its ``controller`` (the JSON of slugs) with the
231        contract it was synthesized from. Each node of the controller is a
232        state, with the values of the inputs and the outputs; the initial
233        states are the nodes that satisfy the initial terms of that contract
234        (slugs does not mark them)."""
235        init = None
236        if isinstance(controller, Result):
237            init = controller.details.get("init")
238            controller = controller.controller
239        if contract is not None:
240            from .gr1 import gr1_kind
241            init = [ltl.to_str(t) for t in list(contract.assumptions) + list(contract.guarantees)
242                    if gr1_kind(t) == "init"]
243        if not isinstance(controller, dict) or "nodes" not in controller:
244            raise ValueError("not a controller of slugs (the JSON of synthesize)")
245        if init is None:
246            raise ValueError("the initial states of a controller need the contract it was "
247                             "synthesized from")
248        names = controller["variables"]
249        nodes = controller["nodes"]
250        order = sorted(nodes, key=int)
251        index = {n: i for i, n in enumerate(order)}
252        # slugs writes an integer as bits x@0.min.max, x@1, ...
253        ints: dict[str, tuple[int, int]] = {}
254        bits: dict[str, list[tuple[int, int]]] = {}
255        plain = []
256        for pos, v in enumerate(names):
257            m = re.fullmatch(r"(.+)@(\d+)(?:\.(-?\d+)\.(-?\d+))?", v)
258            if m:
259                base = m.group(1)
260                if m.group(3) is not None:
261                    ints[base] = (int(m.group(3)), int(m.group(4)))
262                bits.setdefault(base, []).append((int(m.group(2)), pos))
263            else:
264                plain.append((v, pos))
265        variables: dict[str, VarType] = {v: "bool" for v, _ in plain}
266        variables.update(ints)
267        if contract is not None:
268            variables.update({v: t for v, t in contract.variables.items() if v in variables})
269
270        def value(state, v):
271            if v in ints:
272                return ints[v][0] + sum(state[pos] << k for k, pos in bits[v])
273            return _smv_value(bool(state[dict(plain)[v]]))
274
275        lines = ["MODULE main", "VAR", f"    chase_node : 0..{max(len(order) - 1, 0)};", "DEFINE"]
276        for v in variables:
277            arms = [f"chase_node = {index[n]} : {value(nodes[n]['state'], v)};" for n in order]
278            lines.append(f"    {v} := case {' '.join(arms)} esac;")
279        trans = []
280        for n in order:
281            succ = sorted({index[str(s)] for s in nodes[n].get("trans", [])})
282            target = "{" + ", ".join(map(str, succ)) + "}" if succ else None
283            trans.append(f"chase_node = {index[n]} : "
284                         + (f"next(chase_node) in {target};" if target else "FALSE;"))
285        lines.append("TRANS case " + " ".join(trans) + " esac;")
286        init_f = ltl.conjunction([ltl.parse(t) for t in init])
287        lines.append(f"INIT {words.to_smv(init_f, variables)};")
288        model = cls(name or "Controller", "\n".join(lines) + "\n", dict(variables), set())
289        model.variables["chase_node"] = (0, max(len(order) - 1, 0))
290        model.source = {"kind": "controller", "controller": controller}
291        return model
292
293    def check_variables(self, needed, what: str, types: Optional[dict] = None) -> None:
294        """The model declares the variables needed, with the same kind of
295        type as in ``types`` (Boolean, integer, real) when given."""
296        missing = sorted(set(needed) - set(self.variables))
297        if missing:
298            raise ValueError(f"the model {self.name} does not declare {missing}, the variables "
299                             f"of {what}")
300        kind = lambda t: "integer" if isinstance(t, tuple) or t == "int" else t  # noqa: E731
301        for v in needed:
302            mine, theirs = self.variables[v], (types or {}).get(v)
303            if theirs is None or mine == "define" or (
304                    kind(mine) not in ("bool", "integer", "real")
305                    and not words.word_type(mine)):
306                continue
307            if kind(mine) != kind(theirs):
308                raise ValueError(f"{v} is {kind(theirs)} in {what} and {kind(mine)} in the "
309                                 f"model {self.name}")
310
311    def to_dict(self) -> dict:
312        return {"name": self.name, "smv": self.smv,
313                "variables": {k: list(v) if isinstance(v, tuple) else v
314                              for k, v in self.variables.items()}}

A state machine as an SMV program (MODULE main, no specification). variables are the variables it declares (VAR, IVAR, FROZENVAR) and defines (DEFINE), with their types; ivars the ones declared IVAR.
