@classmethod
def from_smv(cls, source: str, name: str | None = None) -> Model: 
126    @classmethod
127    def from_smv(cls, source: str, name: Optional[str] = None) -> "Model":
128        """A model from SMV text or the path of an SMV file. The module main
129        holds the variables of the contracts it is checked against; it must
130        not have specifications (LTLSPEC, SPEC, ...)."""
131        text = source
132        if "MODULE" not in source and os.path.exists(source):
133            with open(source) as f:
134                text = f.read()
135            name = name or os.path.splitext(os.path.basename(source))[0]
136        variables, ivars = {}, set()
137        for kw, start, stop in _sections(text):
138            if kw in _SPECS:
139                raise ValueError(f"the SMV model has a specification ({kw}): CHASE adds the "
140                                 "specification of each check")
141            if kw in ("VAR", "IVAR", "FROZENVAR"):
142                for m in _DECL.finditer(_strip_comments(text)[start:stop]):
143                    variables[m.group(1)] = _vartype(m.group(2))
144                    if kw == "IVAR":
145                        ivars.add(m.group(1))
146            elif kw == "DEFINE":
147                for m in re.finditer(r"([A-Za-z_][\w$#-]*)\s*:=", _strip_comments(text)[start:stop]):
148                    variables.setdefault(m.group(1), "define")
149        model = cls(name or "M", text, variables, ivars)
150        model.source = {"kind": "smv"}
151        return model

@classmethod
def from_dict(cls, d: dict) -> Model: 
160    @classmethod
161    def from_dict(cls, d: dict) -> "Model":
162        """A model from a state machine in JSON::
163
164            {"name": "Arbiter",
165             "inputs": {"req": "bool"}, "outputs": {"grant": "bool"},
166             "states": ["idle", "busy"], "initial": "idle",
167             "transitions": [
168               {"from": "idle", "when": "req", "outputs": {"grant": true}, "to": "busy"},
169               {"from": "idle", "when": "!req", "outputs": {"grant": false}, "to": "idle"},
170               {"from": "busy", "outputs": {"grant": false}, "to": "idle"}]}
171
172        At each step the environment sets the inputs; in its state, the
173        machine takes a transition whose ``when`` (a formula over the inputs
174        and the outputs, true when absent) holds, sets the outputs of the
175        same step as ``outputs`` says (an output not given is free), and
176        moves to ``to`` for the next step. ``initial`` is a state or a list
177        of states. The types are those of ``Contract.from_dict``: "bool",
178        or [min, max] for an integer range. With no transition to take, the
179        machine refuses the input (see ``is_receptive``).
180        """
181        name = d.get("name", "M")
182        inputs = {k: tuple(v) if isinstance(v, list) else v for k, v in d.get("inputs", {}).items()}
183        outputs = {k: tuple(v) if isinstance(v, list) else v
184                   for k, v in d.get("outputs", {}).items()}
185        states = list(d.get("states", []))
186        for s in states:
187            if not _NAME.match(s) or s in ("TRUE", "FALSE"):
188                raise ValueError(f"state {s!r}: the states must be identifiers")
189        if not states:
190            raise ValueError("the state machine has no states")
191        initial = d.get("initial", states[0])
192        initial = [initial] if isinstance(initial, str) else list(initial)
193        for s in initial:
194            if s not in states:
195                raise ValueError(f"the initial state {s!r} is not a state")
196        variables = {**inputs, **outputs}
197        cases = []
198        for i, t in enumerate(d.get("transitions", [])):
199            src, dst = t.get("from"), t.get("to")
200            if src not in states or dst not in states:
201                raise ValueError(f"transition {i}: from and to must be states")
202            parts = [f"chase_state = {src}"]
203            if t.get("when") not in (None, "", "true"):
204                when = ltl.parse(t["when"]) if isinstance(t["when"], str) else t["when"]
205                bad = ltl.variables(when) - set(variables)
206                if bad:
207                    raise ValueError(f"transition {i}: undeclared variables {sorted(bad)}")
208                if _has_temporal(when):
209                    raise ValueError(f"transition {i}: when must not have temporal operators")
210                parts.append(words.to_smv(when, variables))
211            for o, v in t.get("outputs", {}).items():
212                if o not in outputs:
213                    raise ValueError(f"transition {i}: {o} is not an output")
214                parts.append(f"{o} = {_smv_value(v, variables.get(o))}")
215            parts.append(f"next(chase_state) = {dst}")
216            cases.append("(" + " & ".join(parts) + ")")
217        lines = ["MODULE main", "VAR", f"    chase_state : {{{', '.join(states)}}};"]
218        lines += [f"    {v} : {_smvtype(t)};" for v, t in variables.items()]
219        lines.append("INIT " + " | ".join(f"chase_state = {s}" for s in initial) + ";")
220        lines.append("TRANS " + (" | ".join(cases) if cases else "FALSE") + ";")
221        model = cls(name, "\n".join(lines) + "\n", dict(variables), set())
222        model.variables["chase_state"] = "{" + ", ".join(states) + "}"
223        model.source = {"kind": "json", "dict": d}
224        return model

 "states": ["idle", "busy"], "initial": "idle",
 "transitions": [
   {"from": "idle", "when": "req", "outputs": {"grant": true}, "to": "busy"},
   {"from": "idle", "when": "!req", "outputs": {"grant": false}, "to": "idle"},
   {"from": "busy", "outputs": {"grant": false}, "to": "idle"}]}

The types are those of Contract.from_dict: "bool", or [min, max] for an integer range. With no transition to take, the machine refuses the input (see is_receptive).

def is_receptive( model, contract: Contract, backend: str = 'auto', timeout: float = 300, **options) -> Result: 
409def is_receptive(model, contract: Contract, backend: str = "auto",
410                 timeout: float = 300, **options) -> Result:
411    """Does the model accept every input that the assumptions of the
412    contract allow? ``receptive``, or ``not_receptive`` with the trace to the
413    state where it refuses an input (``details``: the ``state`` and the
414    ``input``), or ``unknown``.
415
416    A model that refuses an input has no behavior with it, so it may
417    implement a contract only because it blocks the inputs (OCRA checks
418    receptiveness with the implementation for this reason). The check: in
419    every reachable state, for every next value of the inputs that the
420    safety assumptions allow, there is a transition with that value from
421    which the model can go on forever; and every initial value of the inputs
422    that the initial assumptions allow starts a behavior. The other
423    assumptions (liveness, or terms on the outputs) are not used, which asks
424    for more inputs than OCRA does. The inputs must be Boolean or integer
425    ranges. Uses the BDD engine of nuXmv or NuSMV (CTL).
426    """
427    from .backends import ADAPTERS
428    m = as_model(model, contract)
429    if m is None:
430        raise TypeError("is_receptive takes a model (Model, SMV text, a controller, or a "
431                        "state machine in JSON)")
432    m.check_variables(contract.inputs, f"the inputs of {contract.name}", contract.variables)
433    inputs = list(contract.inputs)
434    domains = {x: _values(contract.inputs[x]) for x in inputs}
435    infinite = [x for x, d in domains.items() if d is None]
436    if infinite:
437        return Result(UNKNOWN, "nusmv", reason=f"the inputs {infinite} are not finite: "
438                      "receptiveness is checked with BDDs")
439    tool = backend.partition("/")[0]   # CTL is checked with BDDs whatever the engine
440    tools = [n for n in (["nuxmv", "nusmv"] if tool == "auto" else [tool])
441             if n in ADAPTERS and hasattr(ADAPTERS[n], "binary")]
442    found = next((ADAPTERS[n].binary() for n in tools if ADAPTERS[n].available()), None)
443    if found is None:
444        return Result(UNKNOWN, backend, reason="neither nuXmv nor NuSMV is installed")
445    path, flavor = found
446
447    probe = lambda x: f"chase_probe_{x}"   # noqa: E731
448    initial, step = _allowed(contract, probe)
449    text = _inputs_as_state(m, set(inputs))
450    lines = [text.rstrip(), "FROZENVAR"]
451    lines += [f"    {probe(x)} : {_smvtype(contract.inputs[x])};" for x in inputs]
452    same = " & ".join(f"{x} = {probe(x)}" for x in inputs) or "TRUE"
453    probes = {**contract.variables, **{probe(x): t for x, t in contract.inputs.items()}}
454    allowed = words.to_smv(ltl.conjunction(step), probes) if step else "TRUE"
455    lines.append(f"SPEC AG (({allowed}) -> EX ({same}));")
456    starts = []
457    count = 1
458    for d in domains.values():
459        count *= len(d)
460    if count <= 1024:
461        for combo in product(*(domains[x] for x in inputs)):
462            v = dict(zip(inputs, combo))
463            if all(_evaluate(t, v, contract.variables) for t in initial):
464                starts.append(v)
465                lines.append("SPEC !(" + (" & ".join(f"{x} = {_smv_value(v[x], contract.inputs[x])}"
466                                                     for x in inputs)
467                                          or "TRUE") + ");")
468    smv = "\n".join(lines) + "\n"
469    start = time.monotonic()
470    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="chase_cps_") as tmp:
471        with open(os.path.join(tmp, "model.smv"), "w") as f:
472            f.write(smv)
473        if flavor == "nuxmv":
474            with open(os.path.join(tmp, "commands"), "w") as f:
475                f.write("set on_failure_script_quits\nread_model -i model.smv\ngo\n"
476                        "check_ctlspec\nquit\n")
477            args = [path, "-source", "commands"]
478        else:
479            args = [path, "-dynamic", "model.smv"]
480        try:
481            proc = subprocess.run(args, cwd=tmp, capture_output=True, text=True,
482                                  stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL, timeout=timeout)
483        except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
484            return Result(UNKNOWN, f"{flavor}/bdd", reason=f"timeout after {timeout:g} s",
485                          seconds=time.monotonic() - start)
486    seconds = time.monotonic() - start
487    backend_name = f"{flavor}/bdd"
488    # The model checkers do not print the verdicts in the order of the file:
489    # the step check is the one with AG, an initial check gives its values.
490    step_chunk, step_verdict, refused = None, None, []
491    for chunk in re.split(r"(?m)^-- specification ", proc.stdout)[1:]:
492        v = re.match(r"(.*?)\s+is (true|false)", chunk, re.S)
493        if not v:
494            continue
495        spec, verdict = " ".join(v.group(1).split()), v.group(2)
496        if spec.startswith("AG"):
497            step_chunk, step_verdict = chunk, verdict
498        elif verdict == "true":     # no initial state with these inputs
499            refused.append({x: _value(val) for x, val in
500                            re.findall(r"(\w+) = (\w+)", spec)})
501    n_specs = len(re.findall(r"(?m)^-- specification ", proc.stdout))
502    if step_verdict is None or n_specs != 1 + len(starts):
503        from .backends.nusmv import _error
504        return Result(UNKNOWN, backend_name, seconds=seconds, details={"model": smv},
505                      reason=_error(proc.stderr + "\n" + proc.stdout) or "no verdict")
506    details: dict[str, Any] = {}
507    if count > 1024:
508        details["initial inputs"] = "not checked: more than 1024 values"
509    from .backends.nusmv import parse_trace
510    if step_verdict == "false":
511        chunks = [step_chunk]
512        names = {**m.variables, **{probe(x): t for x, t in contract.inputs.items()}}
513        trace = parse_trace(chunks[0], names)
514        last = trace.prefix[-1] if trace and trace.prefix else {}
515        blocked = {x: last.get(probe(x)) for x in inputs}
516        state = {k: v for k, v in last.items() if not k.startswith("chase_probe_")}
517        if trace is not None:
518            for s in trace.prefix:
519                for x in inputs:
520                    s.pop(probe(x), None)
521        details.update({"state": state, "input": blocked})
522        return Result(NOT_RECEPTIVE, backend_name, trace=trace, seconds=seconds,
523                      details=details)
524    if refused:
525        details["input"] = refused[0]
526        details["state"] = "initial"
527        return Result(NOT_RECEPTIVE, backend_name, seconds=seconds, details=details)
528    return Result(RECEPTIVE, backend_name, seconds=seconds, details=details)

Does the model accept every input that the assumptions of the contract allow? receptive, or not_receptive with the trace to the state where it refuses an input (details: the state and the input), or unknown.

A model that refuses an input has no behavior with it, so it may implement a contract only because it blocks the inputs (OCRA checks receptiveness with the implementation for this reason). The check: in every reachable state, for every next value of the inputs that the safety assumptions allow, there is a transition with that value from which the model can go on forever; and every initial value of the inputs that the initial assumptions allow starts a behavior. The other assumptions (liveness, or terms on the outputs) are not used, which asks for more inputs than OCRA does. The inputs must be Boolean or integer ranges. Uses the BDD engine of nuXmv or NuSMV (CTL).

def implies( phi, psi, variables: dict[str, str | tuple], backend: str = 'auto', context=None, **options) -> Result: 
68def implies(phi, psi, variables: dict[str, VarType], backend: str = "auto",
69            context=None, **options) -> Result:
70    """Is phi -> psi valid? ``valid``, or ``invalid`` with a counterexample trace
71    (a behavior satisfying phi and violating psi)."""
72    k = _context(context, variables)
73    return backends.check(Implies(_within(k, _formula(phi)), _formula(psi), dict(variables)),
74                          backend, **options)

Is phi -> psi valid? valid, or invalid with a counterexample trace (a behavior satisfying phi and violating psi).

def is_satisfiable( phi, variables: dict[str, str | tuple], backend: str = 'auto', core: bool = False, context=None, **options) -> Result: 
131def is_satisfiable(phi, variables: dict[str, VarType], backend: str = "auto",
132                   core: bool = False, context=None, **options) -> Result:
133    """Is phi satisfiable? ``sat`` with a witness trace, or ``unsat``. With
134    core, an unsat result carries ``unsat_core`` of the conjuncts of phi."""
135    k = _context(context, variables)
136    r = backends.check(Satisfiable(_within(k, _formula(phi)), dict(variables)), backend,
137                       **options)
138    if core and r.status == UNSAT:
139        r.core = unsat_core(_formula(phi), variables, backend, context=k, **options)
140    return r

Is phi satisfiable? sat with a witness trace, or unsat. With core, an unsat result carries unsat_core of the conjuncts of phi.

def unsat_core( formulas, variables: dict[str, str | tuple] | None = None, backend: str = 'auto', context=None, **options) -> Core: 
228def unsat_core(formulas, variables: Optional[dict[str, VarType]] = None,
229               backend: str = "auto", context=None, **options) -> Core:
230    """A minimal set of terms that cannot hold together.
231
232    ``unsat_core(contract)`` searches the assumptions and the guarantees of
233    the contract (A & G) and returns a contract with the terms of the core:
234    its assumptions alone mean the contract is incompatible, its guarantees
235    alone that they contradict each other, both that the guarantees cannot
236    hold when the assumptions do. ``unsat_core(formulas, variables)`` takes
237    a list of formulas, or one formula split at its conjunctions. The
238    context (see ``chase_cps.checks``) holds in every check and is not part
239    of the core: an empty core means that the context alone cannot hold.
240    """
241    if isinstance(formulas, Contract):
242        c = formulas
243        terms = list(c.assumptions) + list(c.guarantees)
244        variables = c.variables
245    else:
246        if variables is None:
247            raise TypeError("unsat_core of formulas needs the variables and their types")
248        c = None
249        terms = _terms(formulas)
250
251    k = _context(context, variables)
252
253    def fails(idx):
254        selected = [terms[i] for i in idx] + ([k] if k is not None else [])
255        r = backends.check(Satisfiable(ltl.conjunction(selected), dict(variables)), backend,
256                           **options)
257        return {UNSAT: True, SAT: False}.get(r.status)
258
259    search = _Search(fails)
260    every = list(range(len(terms)))
261    if not search.fails(every):
262        return Core(UNKNOWN if search.reason else NONE, reason=search.reason,
263                    checks=search.checks)
264    core = search.ddmin(every, [])
265    if search.reason:
266        return Core(UNKNOWN, reason=search.reason, checks=search.checks)
267    if c is None:
268        return Core(FOUND, [terms[i] for i in core], checks=search.checks)
269    na = len(c.assumptions)
270    return Core(FOUND, Contract(f"{c.name}_core", dict(c.inputs), dict(c.outputs),
271                                [terms[i] for i in core if i < na],
272                                [terms[i] for i in core if i >= na]),
273                checks=search.checks)

A minimal set of terms that cannot hold together.

unsat_core(contract) searches the assumptions and the guarantees of the contract (A & G) and returns a contract with the terms of the core: its assumptions alone mean the contract is incompatible, its guarantees alone that they contradict each other, both that the guarantees cannot hold when the assumptions do. unsat_core(formulas, variables) takes a list of formulas, or one formula split at its conjunctions. The context (see chase_cps.checks) holds in every check and is not part of the core: an empty core means that the context alone cannot hold.

def is_realizable( contract: Contract, backend: str = 'auto', core: bool = False, **options) -> Result: 
48def is_realizable(contract: Contract, backend: str = "auto", core: bool = False,
49                  **options) -> Result:
50    """GR(1) realizability of the contract: ``realizable``, or ``unrealizable``
51    with the counter-strategy of the environment. With core, an unrealizable
52    result carries ``unrealizable_core`` of the contract."""
53    _no_context(options, "is_realizable")
54    r = backends.check(Realizable(contract), backend, **options)
55    if core and r.status == UNREALIZABLE:
56        r.core = unrealizable_core(contract, backend=backend, **options)

60def synthesize(contract: Contract, backend: str = "auto", **options) -> Result:
61    """GR(1) synthesis: ``realizable`` with the controller, or ``unrealizable``

def unrealizable_core( guarantees, inputs=None, outputs=None, assumptions=(), backend: str = 'auto', **options) -> Core: 
451def unrealizable_core(guarantees, inputs=None, outputs=None, assumptions=(),
452                      backend: str = "auto", **options) -> Core:
453    """A minimal set of guarantees that is unrealizable under all the
454    assumptions (GR(1), with slugs).
455
456    ``unrealizable_core(contract)`` returns a contract with the assumptions
457    and the guarantees of the core. ``unrealizable_core(guarantees, inputs,
458    outputs, assumptions)`` takes formulas and returns the formulas of the
459    core; inputs and outputs are needed, since realizability depends on who
460    controls each variable.
461    """
462    _no_context(options, "unrealizable_core")
463    if isinstance(guarantees, Contract):
464        c, from_contract = guarantees, True
465    else:
466        if inputs is None or outputs is None:
467            raise TypeError("unrealizable_core of formulas needs the inputs and the outputs")
468        c = Contract.from_strings(inputs=inputs, outputs=outputs,
469                                  assumptions=_terms(assumptions) if assumptions else [],
470                                  guarantees=_terms(guarantees), name="C")
471        from_contract = False
472    terms = list(c.guarantees)
473    problem = gr1_roles(c)
474    if problem:
475        return Core(UNKNOWN, reason=problem)
476    kinds = [gr1_kind(t) for t in terms]
477    env_other = [t for t in c.assumptions if gr1_kind(t) != "justice"]
478
479    def fails(idx):
480        g = [terms[i] for i in idx]
481        # Without justice guarantees the justice assumptions play no role
482        # (QuickCore); leaving them out makes the check cheaper.
483        a = c.assumptions if any(kinds[i] == "justice" for i in idx) else env_other
484        r = backends.check(Realizable(Contract(c.name, dict(c.inputs), dict(c.outputs),
485                                               list(a), g)),
486                           backend, counter_strategy=False, **options)
487        return {UNREALIZABLE: True, REALIZABLE: False}.get(r.status)
488
489    search = _Search(fails)
490    init = [i for i, k in enumerate(kinds) if k == "init"]
491    safety = [i for i, k in enumerate(kinds) if k == "safety"]
492    justice = [i for i, k in enumerate(kinds) if k == "justice"]
493    if not search.fails(init + safety + justice):
494        return Core(UNKNOWN if search.reason else NONE, reason=search.reason,
495                    checks=search.checks)
496    justice = search.ddmin(justice, init + safety)
497    safety = search.ddmin(safety, init + justice)
498    init = search.ddmin(init, safety + justice)
499    if search.reason:
500        return Core(UNKNOWN, reason=search.reason, checks=search.checks)
501    core = [terms[i] for i in sorted(init + safety + justice)]
502    if not from_contract:
503        return Core(FOUND, core, checks=search.checks)
504    return Core(FOUND, Contract(f"{c.name}_core", dict(c.inputs), dict(c.outputs),
505                                list(c.assumptions), core), checks=search.checks)

A minimal set of guarantees that is unrealizable under all the assumptions (GR(1), with slugs).

unrealizable_core(contract) returns a contract with the assumptions and the guarantees of the core. unrealizable_core(guarantees, inputs, outputs, assumptions) takes formulas and returns the formulas of the core; inputs and outputs are needed, since realizability depends on who controls each variable.

def is_well_separated( assumptions, inputs=None, outputs=None, guarantees=(), with_guarantees: bool = True, core: bool = False, backend: str = 'auto', **options) -> Result: 
 67def is_well_separated(assumptions, inputs=None, outputs=None, guarantees=(),
 68                      with_guarantees: bool = True, core: bool = False,
 69                      backend: str = "auto", **options) -> Result:
 70    """Can the component be forced to win by making the environment violate
 71    its assumptions? ``separated`` when it cannot, ``not_separated`` with the
 72    ``controller`` that forces the violation, or ``unknown``.
 73
 74    Takes a contract, or the assumptions with the inputs and the outputs.
 75    The check is GR(1) realizability with slugs of the system specification
 76    (safe(G), {false}): the component must keep its initial and safety
 77    guarantees while it forces the violation (Klein and Pnueli, HVC 2010;
 78    Maoz and Ringert, FSE 2016, Def. 4). A violation that the component can
 79    force only by breaking its own guarantees is not a defect of the
 80    assumptions. With ``with_guarantees=False`` the guarantees are left out,
 81    as in Def. 2 (the default before 0.3.2). Only the case where the violation
 82    can be forced from every initial state is detected (P-all): slugs does
 83    not give the winning region needed for the case of some reachable state.
 84    With core, a ``not_separated`` result carries a minimal set of
 85    assumptions that is still not separated.
 86    """
 87    _no_context(options, "is_well_separated")
 88    if isinstance(assumptions, Contract):
 89        c = assumptions
 90    else:
 91        if inputs is None or outputs is None:
 92            raise TypeError("is_well_separated of formulas needs the inputs and the outputs")
 93        c = Contract.from_strings(inputs=inputs, outputs=outputs,
 94                                  assumptions=_terms(assumptions) if assumptions else [],
 95                                  guarantees=_terms(guarantees) if guarantees else [],
 96                                  name="C")
 97    for t in list(c.assumptions) + (list(c.guarantees) if with_guarantees else []):
 98        if gr1_kind(t) is None:
 99            return Result(UNKNOWN, "slugs", reason=f"not a GR(1) term: {ltl.to_str(t)}")
100    kept = [t for t in c.guarantees
101            if gr1_kind(t) in ("init", "safety")] if with_guarantees else []
102    goal = kept + [ltl.Unary("G", ltl.Unary("F", ltl.Const(False)))]
103
104    def query(a, controller):
105        return backends.check(Realizable(Contract(c.name, dict(c.inputs), dict(c.outputs),
106                                                  list(a), goal)),
107                              backend, controller=controller, counter_strategy=False,
108                              **options)
109
110    r = query(c.assumptions, True)
111    if r.status == REALIZABLE:
112        r.status = NOT_SEPARATED
113    elif r.status == UNREALIZABLE:
114        r.status = SEPARATED
115    if core and r.status == NOT_SEPARATED:
116        terms = list(c.assumptions)
117        search = _Search(lambda idx: {REALIZABLE: True, UNREALIZABLE: False}.get(
118            query([terms[i] for i in idx], False).status))
119        found = search.ddmin(list(range(len(terms))), [])
120        if search.reason:
121            r.core = Core(UNKNOWN, reason=search.reason, checks=search.checks)
122        else:
123            sub = [terms[i] for i in found]
124            r.core = Core(FOUND, Contract(f"{c.name}_core", dict(c.inputs),
125                                                      dict(c.outputs), sub, [])
126                                if isinstance(assumptions, Contract) else sub,
127                                checks=search.checks)
128    return r

Can the component be forced to win by making the environment violate its assumptions? separated when it cannot, not_separated with the controller that forces the violation, or unknown.

Takes a contract, or the assumptions with the inputs and the outputs. The check is GR(1) realizability with slugs of the system specification (safe(G), {false}): the component must keep its initial and safety guarantees while it forces the violation (Klein and Pnueli, HVC 2010; Maoz and Ringert, FSE 2016, Def. 4). A violation that the component can force only by breaking its own guarantees is not a defect of the assumptions. With with_guarantees=False the guarantees are left out, as in Def. 2 (the default before 0.3.2). Only the case where the violation can be forced from every initial state is detected (P-all): slugs does not give the winning region needed for the case of some reachable state. With core, a not_separated result carries a minimal set of assumptions that is still not separated.

def is_vacuous( contract: Contract, outputs=None, core: bool = False, backend: str = 'auto', **options) -> OutputVacuity: 
286def is_vacuous(contract: Contract, outputs=None, core: bool = False, backend: str = "auto",
287               **options) -> OutputVacuity:
288    """Does the contract let the component win without using an output that
289    a liveness guarantee asks for? Vacuity in synthesis, as a strengthening
290    of the guarantees (Bloem, Chockler, Ebrahimi, and Strichman, FMSD 2021):
291
292    - never: Real(A, G + {G !y}), a winning strategy never sets y, so the
293      guarantee that names y is discharged by the assumptions;
294    - eventually: Real(A, G + {!p, G (p -> X p), G (p -> !y), G F p}) with a
295      fresh output p, a winning strategy stops setting y forever from some
296      step on (checked only when ``never`` fails).
297
298    Two weaker formulations are not used. The test on a controller M of
299    Kupferman and Vardi, M & A -> phi[y <- false], and the rewrite
300    Real(A, G[y <- false]) both call a good controller vacuous when an
301    assumption ties the release of the environment to y, such as
302    G ((req & grant) -> X !req): the controller grants, the release
303    follows, and phi[grant <- false] holds because it granted. Forcing y to
304    be false in the behavior asks the right question.
305
306    The outputs checked are ``outputs``, or by default those that occur
307    only positively in a justice guarantee. ``vacuous`` gives each vacuous
308    output with the strategy that wins without it; with core, also a
309    minimal set of the temporal assumptions under which it still wins (the
310    initial assumptions are always kept). The contract must be GR(1) and
311    realizable: otherwise the status is ``unknown`` or ``unrealizable``.
312    """
313    _no_context(options, "is_vacuous")
314    c = contract
315    why = gr1_roles(c)
316    if why:
317        return OutputVacuity(UNKNOWN, reason=why)
318    named = _liveness_outputs(c)
319    if outputs is None:
320        targets = list(named)
321    else:
322        targets = [outputs] if isinstance(outputs, str) else list(outputs)
323        for y in targets:
324            if y not in c.outputs:
325                raise ValueError(f"{y} is not an output of {c.name}")
326    start = time.monotonic()
327    base = is_realizable(c, backend, **options)
328    if base.status != REALIZABLE:
329        return OutputVacuity(base.status, checked=targets, seconds=time.monotonic() - start,
330                             reason=base.reason or ("the contract is unrealizable"
331                                                    if base.status == UNREALIZABLE else ""))
332    out = OutputVacuity(NOT_VACUOUS, checked=targets)
333    unknown = []
334
335    def strengthened(y, mode, assumptions):
336        if mode == "never":
337            return Contract(c.name, dict(c.inputs), dict(c.outputs), list(assumptions),
338                            list(c.guarantees) + [ltl.parse(f"G !{y}")])
339        p = f"parked_{y}"
340        while p in c.variables:
341            p = "_" + p
342        extra = [f"!{p}", f"G ({p} -> X {p})", f"G ({p} -> !{y})", f"G F {p}"]
343        return Contract(c.name, dict(c.inputs), {**c.outputs, p: "bool"}, list(assumptions),
344                        list(c.guarantees) + [ltl.parse(f) for f in extra])
345
346    def realizable(y, mode, assumptions, controller=False):
347        return backends.check(Realizable(strengthened(y, mode, assumptions)), backend,
348                              controller=controller, counter_strategy=False, **options)
349
350    for y in targets:
351        for mode in ("never", "eventually"):
352            r = realizable(y, mode, c.assumptions, controller=True)
353            if r.status == REALIZABLE:
354                v = VacuousOutput(y, mode, named.get(y, []), r.controller)
355                if core:
356                    v.core = _assumption_core(c, lambda a, y=y, mode=mode:
357                                              realizable(y, mode, a).status)
358                out.vacuous.append(v)
359                break
360            if r.status != UNREALIZABLE:
361                unknown.append(f"{y}: {r.reason or r.status}")
362                break
363    if out.vacuous:
364        out.status = VACUOUS
365    elif unknown:
366        out.status, out.reason = UNKNOWN, "; ".join(unknown)
367    out.seconds = time.monotonic() - start
368    return out

Does the contract let the component win without using an output that a liveness guarantee asks for? Vacuity in synthesis, as a strengthening of the guarantees (Bloem, Chockler, Ebrahimi, and Strichman, FMSD 2021):

  • never: Real(A, G + {G !y}), a winning strategy never sets y, so the guarantee that names y is discharged by the assumptions;
  • eventually: Real(A, G + {!p, G (p -> X p), G (p -> !y), G F p}) with a fresh output p, a winning strategy stops setting y forever from some step on (checked only when never fails).

Two weaker formulations are not used. The test on a controller M of Kupferman and Vardi, M & A -> phi[y <- false], and the rewrite Real(A, G[y <- false]) both call a good controller vacuous when an assumption ties the release of the environment to y, such as G ((req & grant) -> X !req): the controller grants, the release follows, and phi[grant <- false] holds because it granted. Forcing y to be false in the behavior asks the right question.

The outputs checked are outputs, or by default those that occur only positively in a justice guarantee. vacuous gives each vacuous output with the strategy that wins without it; with core, also a minimal set of the temporal assumptions under which it still wins (the initial assumptions are always kept). The contract must be GR(1) and realizable: otherwise the status is unknown or unrealizable.

@dataclass
class System: 
34@dataclass
35class System:
36    """Components connected by the names of their variables, and the
37    contract of the system. ``status`` is the result of the last check of
38    the composition against the contract of the system, or None."""
39
40    name: str
41    components: list = field(default_factory=list)
42    contract: Optional[Contract] = None
43    status: Optional[str] = None
44
45    def composition(self, discharge: bool = False, **options) -> Contract:
46        """The composition of the contracts of the components."""
47        if not self.components:
48            raise ValueError(f"system {self.name} has no component")
49        result = self.components[0].contract
50        for c in self.components[1:]:
51            result = result.compose(c.contract, name=self.name, discharge=discharge, **options)
52        return result
53
54    def connections(self) -> list[tuple[str, str, str]]:
55        """(driver, reader, variable) for each output of a component read by
56        another one."""
57        out = []
58        for d in self.components:
59            for r in self.components:
60                if d is not r:
61                    out += [(d.name, r.name, v) for v in d.contract.outputs
62                            if v in r.contract.inputs]
63        return out
64
65    def check(self, discharge: bool = False, backend: str = "auto", **options) -> dict:
66        """Checks each implementation against its contract, and the
67        composition against the contract of the system; sets the statuses
68        and returns them by name (the system under its own name)."""
69        from .checks import is_implementation, refines
70        statuses = {}
71        for c in self.components:
72            if c.implementation is not None:
73                c.status = is_implementation(c.implementation, c.contract, backend=backend,
74                                             **options).status
75                statuses[c.name] = c.status
76        if self.contract is not None:
77            self.status = refines(self.composition(discharge, backend=backend, **options),
78                                  self.contract, backend=backend, **options).status
79            statuses[self.name] = self.status
80        return statuses
81
82    def _repr_html_(self) -> str:
83        from .viz import notebook
84        return notebook(self)

112@dataclass
113class Result:
114    """The answer of a back end.
115
116    status is valid or invalid (implication), sat or unsat (satisfiability),
117    realizable or unrealizable, or unknown with the reason (e.g. a timeout,
118    or no back end installed). A Result is true when the property holds.
119    """
120    status: str
121    backend: str = ""
122    trace: Optional[Trace] = None        # counterexample or witness
123    controller: Optional[Any] = None     # synthesized strategy
124    counter_strategy: Optional[Any] = None   # of the environment, when unrealizable
125    reason: str = ""                     # why the result is unknown
126    seconds: float = 0.0
127    details: dict = field(default_factory=dict)
128    core: Optional[Any] = None           # with core=True: the Core explaining a failure
129    reals: Optional[str] = None          # with real variables: regions, smt, or predicates
130
131    def __bool__(self) -> bool:
132        return self.status in (VALID, SAT, REALIZABLE, SEPARATED, RECEPTIVE)
133
134    def to_dict(self) -> dict:
135        d = {"status": self.status, "backend": self.backend, "seconds": round(self.seconds, 3)}
136        if self.trace is not None:
137            d["trace"] = self.trace.to_dict()
138        if self.controller is not None:
139            d["controller"] = self.controller
140        if self.counter_strategy is not None:
141            d["counter_strategy"] = self.counter_strategy
142        if self.core is not None:
143            d["core"] = self.core.to_dict()
144        if self.reals is not None:
145            d["reals"] = self.reals
146        if self.reason:
147            d["reason"] = self.reason
148        if self.details:
149            d["details"] = self.details
150        return d

@dataclass
class Trace: 
 90@dataclass
 91class Trace:
 92    """A lasso-shaped trace: the prefix, then the loop repeated forever.
 93
 94    Each state maps every variable to its value.
 95    """
 96    prefix: list[dict[str, Any]]
 97    loop: list[dict[str, Any]]
 98
 99    def to_dict(self) -> dict:
100        def state(s):
101            return {k: _json_value(v) for k, v in s.items()}
102        return {"prefix": [state(s) for s in self.prefix], "loop": [state(s) for s in self.loop]}
103
104    def __str__(self) -> str:
105        rows = []
106        for i, s in enumerate(self.prefix + self.loop):
107            mark = "  <- loop starts" if self.loop and i == len(self.prefix) else ""
108            rows.append(f"  {i}: " + ", ".join(f"{k}={v}" for k, v in s.items()) + mark)
109        return "\n".join(rows)

def check(query, backend: str = 'auto', **options) -> Result: 
38def check(query, backend: str = "auto", **options) -> Result:
39    """Answer a query with the given back end, or the first available one.
40
41    With backend "auto", the environment variable CHASE_BACKEND, when set,
42    names the back end to use for the queries it answers. A back end may name
43    its engine, as in "nuxmv/bdd" (see ``chase_cps.backends.nusmv``). A query with real
44    variables goes through ``chase_cps.reals``; the others go straight to the
45    back ends.
46    """
47    from .. import reals
48    from ..queries import Holds
49    if not isinstance(query, Holds) and reals.has_real_variables(query):
50        return reals.check(query, backend, **options)
51    return dispatch(query, backend, **options)
